Colorism is real inside the umbrella. Intra-Latino hierarchy is real: Mexican default in this state will talk over a Maya or Caribbean household if you let it.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Who speaks in the meeting, who holds the papers, who is allowed to leave the house — ask, and follow law. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Latinos exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it familismo. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Uninsured and delayed-care patterns sit in this umbrella. Date Minnesota figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate on this page.

### Access

Compass Mexican poverty (ACS 2019–2023) is 12.8 percent — a poverty figure, not an uninsured rate, not the whole umbrella. Pattern now: people delay, people use the emergency room as the door, people skip follow-up when the lobby feels like enforcement.

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish or this indigenous language — these are clinical events. When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening because a stereotype said this community is dramatic, or stoic, or “they take care of their own.” Do not fold this history into Tuskegee (African American literacy) or into a generic “immigrant mistrust” slide. This community’s medical mistrust also runs through camps and war in some streams, dismissals, and child-protection fear.

Traditional healers, yerberías, and parish prayer can sit next to a fierce wish for biomedicine. If they name a healer, listen. Do not make the healer the case plan unless they asked. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter in a health encounter.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Latino Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish, evangelical, and family climates can mean silence, exile, or danger. That is not every family.

### This person

Familismo can be protection and can be pressure. You do not get to decide which one this household is from the doorway.

Staff duty: use the name they use. Do not out them to an elder, a parish, or a “supportive family” you invented as cultural humility. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a family-values exhibit.

Afro-Latino and indigenous queer people exist inside this page. Do not mash them into the historic African American LGBTQ chapter, and do not bleach them. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
There is no Latino uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota.

### Dress

Indigenous traje and Maya dress are public at fiesta and ceremony, not a daily costume, and not yours to request for a Heritage Month photo. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

Colorism and hair texture are real inside the umbrella. Afro-Latino hair is not the CROWN Act chapter copied over — and you still do not touch, still do not police, still do not treat tightness or looseness as a professionalism problem. Mestizo default beauty is a hierarchy. Name it if it is in the room. Do not rank.

Quinceañera dress, baptism white, funeral black, evangelical modesty, Catholic veil in some rooms — celebration and devotion, not a case note. Do not touch. Do not rank piety or indigeneity off clothing. Ask the person, with gender match if they want it.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Not one playlist. Mariachi, ranchera, norteño, banda, cumbia, salsa, merengue, bachata, vallenato, música andina, marimba, corridos, reggaeton, church music — origin names the sound.

### Variation

A Mexican default playlist in a Guatemalan or Puerto Rican waiting room is the mash in speakers.

Corridos include narcocorridos in some streams. That is a named fact, not a joke and not a risk score you write on a last name.

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. Church music is not staff entertainment. Knowing that music is public life will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating one Heritage Month speaker as the community.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Fútbol is the default public sport for many boys and men, and for many girls. Boxing has prestige in some streams. Baseball and softball show up especially in Caribbean households. School sport is ordinary for the second generation.

### Not the whole person

Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

Leagues and pickup games are social infrastructure in metro and in plant towns. They are not a substitute for language access on a waiver. They are not consultation.

World Cup and club fútbol are public life. A viewing party is not community engagement. Sport clubs are not the interpreter pool.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Spanish-language literature is world literature. That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish.

### Literacy in the lobby

Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Indigenous oral literature — Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, and others — is older than the Spanish file and is not “no letters.”

Minnesota has Latino journalists, poets, and scholars. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know this is not a people without letters, and not a people who can all read the exception process.

Print Spanish from Spain, Mexico, or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish. CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Murals on the West Side and on Lake Street are public Minnesota art, not a booth. Ofrendas at Día de los Muertos are public history. Textiles and indigenous weaving are art and memory, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. Do not photograph an altar because it is pretty. An ofrenda is not a case plan. A mural tour is not consultation.

Contemporary Latino and indigenous artists work in this state. Knowing that will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating the umbrella as a people without a public culture — and from treating that public culture as engagement.

sections.heading: Labor, War, Enforcement, and the State
sections.body:
There is no single Civil Rights Movement to copy onto this page. The political literacy here is stacked.

### The badge

U.S. labor recruitment; IRCA 1986 and settlement; Mexican and Central American displacement; Salvadoran civil war and TPS; Guatemalan war and Maya flight; Nicaraguan streams; Cuban and Venezuelan political flight (date those if you cite); Puerto Rican colonial status and citizenship without treating that household as foreign; and U.S. enforcement that reorganizes Tuesday.

When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. A DHS badge is not automatically help. That is not paranoia. It is pattern. Do not tell people the climate is fine so the form is fair now. Do not use a civil war or a raid as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate crossing for your professional development.

Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Notices to a household that will not open the door are a closed gate with a polite label. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a deportation score.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Food processing, dairy, agriculture, construction, service, restaurants, cleaning, childcare, home care, professional second generation, public employment.

### Work

Rural plants and metro kitchens can sit in the same extended family. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same household.

Worker centers and parishes may be the trusted channel in Greater Minnesota. Name the local one. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume CLUES reaches a dairy county. Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice.

### Staff

Latino staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters, not the indigenous-language pool, and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan. Do not make a Latino colleague your unpaid tutor.

Remittance to kin in another country is obligation for many, not a disposable luxury. A budget that treats it as optional has already chosen a household type. Puerto Rican households may be sending money to the island after disaster — still not an immigration script.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Language including indigenous. Book qualified Spanish AND ask.

### Language

Confirm Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna when that is the home language. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

Who is in the room. Gender match in maternal and intimate care if they want it. Titles. Two surnames. SSN on the first screen: if you do not need it, do not demand it as theater. Mixed-status: do not collect status you do not need. Enforcement climate: skipped appointments are pattern.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. If they name a healer or a parish, listen. Do not make either the case plan unless they asked. Mandated reporting still exists. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. You follow the law. You still see a family.

Rural access is a gate: distance, clinic hours, one interpreter contracted from the Cities who does not speak this language. Open the rural brief beside this page. A nuclear form that cannot see grandparents as the household is already a who.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not Brazilian Portuguese-only. Brazilian Minnesota is adjacent. Open a different door. Do not file Portuguese under Spanish and call it CLAS.

### Adjacent doors

Not “Spanish” as indigenous. Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna are not dialects of Spanish. A Spanish interpreter is not those languages.

Puerto Rican is U.S. citizenship. Do not run an immigration script by default. Cuban, Dominican, Ecuadorian, Colombian, Salvadoran, Guatemalan, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Venezuelan, Mexican — name the origin. The Mexican default is a Minnesota fact and a Minnesota harm when it becomes the only file.

Not Somali. Not historic African American. Afro-Latino people exist — ask, do not mash them into the African American brief because both are Black, and do not bleach them into a mestizo Latino blob. Filipino Spanish-colonial history is not this page. Open the people brief that matches this household. Never one Latino module.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Mexican cultural community.

### Counts

229,576; Twin Cities 61.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent; foreign-born 26.7 percent; language other than English (age 5+) 58.3 percent; English less than “very well” 23.7 percent; poverty 12.8 percent; median household income about $66,000. Mixtec, Zapotec may be in the home — Compass notes the language possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count.

Same Compass vintage, other origin profiles: Colombian 9,431; Cuban 9,406; Ecuadorian 18,271 (indigenous languages may be in the home); Guatemalan 17,172 (nearly half Greater Minnesota — K’iche’, Mam, other Mayan); Puerto Rican 21,802 (U.S. citizens); Salvadoran 17,571 (civil war and TPS history). Venezuelan, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Dominican and others live here — pattern now, date if you cite. Do not invent those counts on this page.

### What the count is not

Do not add these profiles into a fake “Latino Minnesota” total. Definitions overlap; people can appear in more than one story; the umbrella is not a people. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and across Hispanic-origin versus ancestry versus language. Date the number you cite.

A rate is not the person. Poverty 12.8 percent (Mexican, that vintage) is not the Guatemalan household in a plant town and not the Puerto Rican household in the Cities. Uninsured and delayed-care patterns: date MN figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
CLUES — Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio — https://clues.org/. Twin Cities services. Not the whole state.

### Public doors

Centro Tyrone Guzmán — family and youth; metro. Rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. The parish in a dairy county may be the actual door.

Minnesota Compass origin profiles (ACS 2019–2023): Mexican, Guatemalan, Puerto Rican, Salvadoran, Ecuadorian, Colombian, Cuban — date the retrieval. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Open the rural brief when place is the gate. Open the African American brief for historic African American households. Open this for a Latino household. Open an indigenous-language request when Spanish is the wrong door.

### Learn on your own time

Do not make a Latino colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC CLUES and call it consultation. Pay partners. Report back. Hispanic Heritage Month is not the work.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna may be in the home. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: two surnames. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

Hour caps, exception processes, SSN on the first screen, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral. Mixed-status households will bounce if the first field feels like enforcement. Do not collect status you do not need.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Enforcement climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. Puerto Rican is citizenship — do not run an immigration script by default.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is part of this picture — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Latino staff are not the interpreter pool, not the indigenous-language pool, and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Latino mash: opening one blob, or Mexican as the only file, because the checkbox says Hispanic is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned the second surname.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about the eleven federally recognized Tribal Nations in Minnesota — seven Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) nations and four Dakota nations. They are governments. Consultation is government-to-government. A culture card is not that door. A land acknowledgment without a call is not that door.

### Who this is

The eleven nations, as named by the Minnesota Indian Affairs Council:

Anishinaabe reservations: Grand Portage (northeast corner); Bois Forte (extreme north); Red Lake (extreme north, west of Bois Forte); White Earth (northwest); Leech Lake (north central); Fond du Lac (northeast, west of Duluth); Mille Lacs (central, south and east of Brainerd).

Dakota communities: Shakopee Mdewakanton (south of the Twin Cities near Prior Lake); Prairie Island (near Red Wing); Lower Sioux (near Redwood Falls); Upper Sioux (near Granite Falls).

Ojibwe and Dakota are distinct languages, territories, legal histories, and governments. The Minnesota Chippewa Tribe is a government of six Anishinaabe reservations — Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, and White Earth. Red Lake is not in that union. Dakota nations are not in it. Filing all eleven as “Chippewa” closes the meeting before it starts.

Minnesota Compass’s Native American profile (ACS 2019–2023) counts about 162,216 people — Twin Cities 44.8 percent, Greater Minnesota 55.2 percent. Compass cannot split that count by nation. The number is not enrollment. It is not the eleven. It is not permission to skip the Office of Indian Policy. Date it if you cite it. It is not government-to-government.

Urban Native Minneapolis–St. Paul is part of this brief. People who live off-reservation for work, school, or kinship remain citizens of nations.

A community portrait here is not one socioeconomic slice. Native Minnesotans are attorneys, physicians, scientists, teachers, nurses, people who work for tribally run health and social programs, urban Indian-health clinicians, artists, language teachers, plant and casino workers, students, and elders. The same is true inside each nation. A casino does not make a people. Poverty on a Compass line does not make a people.

### Who this is not

Alaska Native people have their own brief. Other U.S. tribal citizens living in Minnesota are not automatically one of the eleven. Mendota Mdewakanton and other communities seeking recognition are not a twelfth nation on this page.

This is not a mash of “communities of color.” Rondo is African American history. Cedar-Riverside is Somali history. Phillips, Little Earth, and the eleven governments are this page.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. Name the nation. Always defer to this family. Always defer to the nation on who belongs to it.

The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well — how kinship is held, what respect looks like, what a greeting carries, what a form may land on. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture. Population size is not culture size. Eleven governments are not a small-count brochure.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Dakota and Anishinaabe peoples are older than Minnesota and older than this department. This land is Dakota homeland in creation stories. It is also a central place in Anishinaabe history — the westward movement along the Great Lakes, wild rice, and the northern forests.

### Anishinaabe

Anishinaabe (also written Ojibwe, Ojibwa, Chippewa in U.S. legal English) is a people across the Great Lakes — Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ontario, and beyond. Ojibwemowin is the language. Bands in this state are nations.

### Dakota

Dakota (Dakhóta) is a people of this prairie and river country, related to Lakota and Nakota — not the same as “Sioux” borrowed from a nineteenth-century statute. Dakota language and Dakota nations in Minnesota survived exile. That sentence is literacy.

### What people brought

Nationhood, language, kinship, land relationship, ceremony, wild rice and water as more than commodities, and a record of dealing with the United States as governments. What they met: a territory and then a state that took children, land, and language, and then wrote English forms.

History is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family. You do not narrate 1862 to a Dakota parent as icebreaker. You do know it. Ojibwe and Dakota are not flavors of one story.

sections.heading: Geography
sections.body:
Name the nation. Geography here is government, not scenery.

### Anishinaabe nations

Bois Forte Band of Chippewa (Zagaakwaandagowiniwag) — extreme northern Minnesota; Nett Lake and Vermilion.

Fond du Lac Band of Lake Superior Chippewa (Nagaajiwanaang) — west of Duluth; Cloquet. Urban Duluth households remain the nation.

Grand Portage Band of Lake Superior Chippewa (Gichi-Onigaming) — northeast corner, Lake Superior, a border.

Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe — north central; Cass Lake.

Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe — central, south and east of Brainerd; Districts I–III as the nation names them.

Red Lake Nation — extreme north, west of Bois Forte; not in the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe union; a distinct land and legal history.

White Earth Nation — northwest; allotment and land restoration are living politics, not a museum.

### Dakota nations

Lower Sioux Indian Community (Cansa’yapi) — near Redwood Falls.

Prairie Island Indian Community — near Red Wing, next to a nuclear generating plant.

Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community — south of the Twin Cities near Prior Lake. Economic position is real and is not the Dakota story copied onto the others.

Upper Sioux Community (Pezihutazizi Oyate) — near Granite Falls.

### Cities and off-reservation life

Urban Native Minneapolis–St. Paul — Phillips, Little Earth, and the metro as a whole. Off-reservation towns near each nation. People who live in Duluth, Bemidji, Cloquet, Onamia, Prior Lake, Redwood Falls, Granite Falls, Red Wing, and ordinary suburbs.

A reservation address is not the only address. Minneapolis is not the only address. Compass Native American: 55.2 percent Greater Minnesota, 44.8 percent Twin Cities (ACS 2019–2023). That split is the opposite of Hmong Minnesota (about 94 percent Twin Cities). Distance, broadband, and county lines are how the work actually runs. Nationhood is not a ZIP code.

A physician enrolled at White Earth who works in Minneapolis is still of that nation. A scientist at a tribal natural-resources office and a student at a tribal college are the same peoplehood as a household using a waiver. Community portrait means all of that.

sections.heading: Migration and Foundational Events
sections.body:
Treaties. Broken treaties. Removal. The U.S.–Dakota War of 1862. The largest mass execution in U.S. history at Mankato on 26 December 1862. Internment at Fort Snelling. Exile of Dakota people from Minnesota. Allotment and the Nelson Act of 1889. Boarding schools. Termination-era policy and restoration. The Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978. The Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act. Haaland v. Brackeen (2023) did not repeal ICWA.

### 1862 and the boarding-school system

If the Great Migration is the foundational demographic event of modern Black America, 1862 and the boarding-school system are foundational events you cannot skip for Dakota and Anishinaabe Minnesota. They are not “in the past.” They are why a county petition can still sound like removal.

### Ordinary movement

People also move for ordinary reasons — work, school, love, health — and remain of their nations. Urban Native Minneapolis is not a leftover. AIM’s founding in Minneapolis in 1968 is Minnesota history.

Boarding school and removal are why mistrust is rational. That is structure. A powwow is public and also nation. It is not the Tuesday on which a county files a petition.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Kinship systems. Othermothers. Extended care. Who cares for the child may not match a nuclear English form.

### Who is family

Aunties, grandparents, clan and tiyospaye relationships, and people who are family without a blood-quantum worksheet — all of that is family. A form that only fits two legal parents in one household cannot see kin.

Ask who should be in the room. A scientist parent, a lawyer aunt, a grandmother who harvests rice, and someone who works for a tribally run program can be the same family. “Broken family” is what the English form says when the household is not nuclear.

### ICWA and MIFPA

The Indian Child Welfare Act and the Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act exist because the state has a record of taking children. Placement preferences, inquiry (“is this child an Indian child?”), notice to the nation, and active efforts are law. Active efforts are documented work with the family’s people, culture, and values — not a box after a removal. Kin search is not optional courtesy.

### Who belongs

You do not decide who is Native. The nation does. Blood quantum is colonial technology. Enrollment versus community belonging is nation business. A lobby quiz is not inquiry.

sections.heading: Minnesota
sections.body:
The Minnesota Indian Affairs Council exists to protect the sovereignty of the eleven and the well-being of American Indian citizens throughout the state — including urban. The DHS Office of Indian Policy is a door inside this department. Tribal-State Relations Training is required for many roles. Take it. A land acknowledgment is not a substitute.

### Governments, not a mailing list

Nations are seats, not a copy line. Notice to nations on the same day as an eList is not consultation. Empty follow-up cells on a tribal notice are a structural failure.

Minnesota-specific institutions — partners, not a list you copy once: each nation’s government; urban Indian organizations including Native American Community Clinic, Division of Indian Work, Ain Dah Yung, American Indian Family Center, MIGIZI; Little Earth; tribal colleges and language tables; urban Indian health. Pay. Report back. You are a guest.

### Staff

Staff of this department include citizens of these nations. They are not unpaid liaisons, unpaid interpreters, or “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan.

Rondo is African American literacy. Cedar-Riverside is Somali literacy. Phillips, Little Earth, and the eleven governments are this page.

sections.heading: Heart of the People
sections.body:
Sovereignty. Land. Kinship. Language. Holistic health — physical, mental, emotional, spiritual as one. Nationhood is the first fact. Culture is not yours to display.

### Peoplehood older than the United States

Du Bois’s double consciousness is African American intelligence. It is not a universal minority sentence to copy here. Dakota and Anishinaabe peoplehood is older than the United States. The tension here is not “how to be both Native and American without bleaching.” It is that the United States and this state made treaties, broke them, took children, and still write English forms. You work that fact. You do not perform it.

### Not a culture club

Eleven governments. Not a club. A Heritage Month frybread lunch is not the heart of anything.

Language revitalization is nationhood. Manoomin (wild rice) is food and law and season. Wacipi / powwow is public and also nation. Ceremony is not a training module. You are a guest even when the meeting is in a county building.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
These concepts recur. They express differently by nation, family, and generation. They are hypotheses — not a script for the person in front of you.

### Sovereignty

Governments, not clubs. Treaties are living legal facts. A nation is not a stakeholder list.

### Treaty

The United States and Minnesota still sit on treaty ground. All seven Anishinaabe reservations in Minnesota were originally established by treaty and are considered separate and distinct nations by the United States government (Minnesota Indian Affairs Council). Dakota communities in this state are nations that survived exile.

### Kinship

Who is family may not fit the form. ICWA and MIFPA placement is the legal expression of that fact in child welfare.

### Language

Ojibwemowin and Dakota language revitalization. English is common. A word you learned in a training is not expertise. Language nests and tribal schools are nationhood, not an interpreter convenience.

### Land and water

Not a backdrop. Hunting, fishing, ricing, and treaty rights are law, not hobbies.

### Ceremony

Nationhood. The American Indian Religious Freedom Act. Not a team-building event. Not a lodge you book as department programming.

### Seven Grandfather Teachings

Wisdom, love, respect, bravery, honesty, humility, truth — these are Anishinaabe. They do not paste onto a Dakota household as a values poster. Dakota ethics and kinship have their own names. Ask.

### Blood quantum

Colonial technology. Enrollment is nation business.

### Two-spirit

Native LGBTQ people exist. Named variation. Not a side note and not a branding exercise.

### Urban Native

Not off the list.

A land acknowledgment is not consultation.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
sections.body:
Traditional practice and Christianity both live here — often in the same family.

### Missions and ceremony

Catholic missions, Episcopal missions, boarding-school Christianity, and traditional ceremony are all Minnesota facts. The American Indian Religious Freedom Act (1978) is law. Ceremony is not a team-building event. Hmong txiv neeb is not a sweat lodge. Dakota lodge is not Anishinaabe lodge by default.

If they name traditional healing, follow their lead and the nation’s. A pastor, a priest, or a healer is the case plan when this family asked. Do not book a lodge as department programming. Do not photograph ceremony.

### Boarding-school harm

Spiritual harm from boarding schools is structure: language forbidden, ceremony punished, children taken. That harm sits in the same clinic as ordinary chronic disease. You can hold both. You do not interrogate a ceremony to complete a field.

A white convert to a lodge is not a citizen of a nation. A Dakota person who is Catholic is still Dakota. Mixing those facts is how the meeting goes wrong.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Follow this room. Handshake is common in many rooms. A protocol invented from a training slide is not a greeting. Do not force a hand. A word you learned is not an icebreaker.

### Elders and titles

Elders first. Listen longer than the form wants. Titles if they use them. Ask how to say a name.

You are a guest in nation space even when the meeting is in a county building. The Black nod is African American intelligence. As-salāmu ʿalaykum is Somali and Muslim intelligence. Importing another community’s greeting is a mash.

### Silence

Silence can be thought, not refusal. Directness is not rudeness. Filling every pause because Minnesota Nice is uncomfortable is not listening.

sections.heading: Naming
sections.body:
Ask how to say it. English names, nation names, and language names may all sit on one person. Enrollment names are nation business.

### Not a quiz

A name is not a blood-quantum quiz. Do not joke. Do not Anglicize. The form that only fits Mary Jones is a gate.

You do not decide who is Native. A scientist named in English and a language teacher named in Ojibwemowin can be siblings. Neither is more authentic as a case note.

Pronounce Bois Forte, Mille Lacs, Shakopee, Pezihutazizi. If you cannot, ask. Literacy includes the map.

sections.heading: Dates and Calendar
sections.body:
Treaty dates. 1862. 26 December — the Mankato executions; literacy, not a holiday you put on a flyer. Boarding-school remembrance. American Indian Month in Minnesota (May, as the state has marked it). Nation days and powwow calendars some families name. Ricing season. Hunting seasons as treaty practice.

### This family’s calendar

A calendar date is literacy. It is not consultation and not a day off the form. “Native holiday” does not belong on a case note. Ask this family and this nation.

Juneteenth is African American literacy. Eid is not this page. Another community’s calendar is not inclusion here.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Boarding-school history is structure in the school building too.

### Schools and colleges

Tribal schools, public schools, language nests, tribal colleges, University of Minnesota and Minnesota State students, attorneys with JDs, physicians, scientists, and teachers.

Bachelor’s or higher among Compass Native American adults 25 and older is 22.5 percent (ACS 2019–2023). High school graduate or higher 88.4 percent. Date it. A rate is not the person.

A degree is not exceptional in a way that insults the rest. Athletics is not the path. Language revitalization is not extra. English-only forms are a gate even when speech is strong.

### Teachers and scholars

Anton Treuer’s public Ojibwe-language work, tribal-college faculty, and classroom teachers in Onamia or Red Lake are the same educational story as a Ph.D. They are not a hierarchy of authenticity.

A parent who speaks Dakota or Ojibwe and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only IEP is the gate.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Listen. Do not photograph ceremony. Hospitality is not consent to extract. Keep medical and legal time.

### Guest

Do not record a lodge. Do not ask for a song as a closer. You are a guest. A design is not a logo for the department.

Food offered in a home is courtesy. You still keep the clock for court and clinic. Frybread is not a personality. Refusing everything as professionalism is not courtesy.

Nation offices are not a research site. Pay. Report back.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.body:
Ojibwe and Dakota language revitalization. English is common.

### What Compass shows

Compass Native American (age 5+): 87.9 percent English only; 12.1 percent a language other than English; 3.2 percent speak English less than very well (ACS 2019–2023). Date it. Low limited-English-proficient numbers on a Compass line are not permission to skip the language an elder asks for.

Book an interpreter if they ask. A word you learned is not expertise. Do not correct English in the lobby.

### Silence and story

Silence can be thought, not refusal. Directness is not rudeness. Story and circular speech can be how an elder thinks in public. A short English yes may be exhaustion. Ask whether they agree. A smile is not consent.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
Blood quantum is colonial technology. Enrollment versus community is nation business. Two-spirit people exist. Data sovereignty is nation business.

### MMIW and child welfare

Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women is current structure, not a poster. The state has a record of taking children. That is why ICWA exists.

Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Mandated reporting still stands.

### Not one economy

Gaming revenue at one nation is not the Dakota story. Poverty on a Compass line is not the Anishinaabe story. Scientists, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and professionals in tribally run programs exist in the same nations as people on waivers. Community portrait means all of that. Dominant culture does not get to choose which slice is “the real Native.”

Haaland v. Brackeen (2023) upheld ICWA. That is current law. The Act is not optional because a commenter was uncomfortable.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Pattern, dated: American Indian Minnesotans have among the worst health outcomes of any group in the state — date the specific rate when you have the controlling Minnesota Department of Health or tribal-epidemiology source. Do not invent a number here to sound complete.

### Compass

Compass Native American (ACS 2019–2023): 16.2 percent with a disability; 8.5 percent without health insurance; median household income about $58,000; 17.9 percent below poverty. Date it. A rate is not the person.

### Systems of care

Indian Health Service, tribal health, urban Indian health, and county clinics are not interchangeable. Olmstead and disability still apply. So does nationhood. Believe reported pain. Historical trauma and ordinary chronic disease sit in the same body. You can hold both.

A physician who is a citizen of White Earth and a patient at an urban Indian clinic are both this page. The clinic is not the whole portrait.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Two-spirit and LGBTQ Native people exist. Harm in some churches and in some traditional rooms. Named variation.

Use the name and pronouns. Outing someone to family or to a nation office is not culture. The people-page rule is the workplace rule.

Two-spirit is not a brand you put on a Heritage Month flyer. It is people.

sections.heading: Hair and Dress
sections.body:
Hair can be spiritual, personal, or neither. Long hair, braids, a ribbon skirt, a jingle dress, a suit in a St. Paul hearing room — all of that is this people. Do not touch. Locs, braids, or long hair are not unprofessional.

CROWN-adjacent harm still happens. Follow this person. A ribbon skirt is not a costume you request.

A lawyer in a ribbon skirt and a scientist in a lab coat are not opposites. They may be the same person on different Tuesdays.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Drum, song, powwow as public and as nation, church music, contemporary Minnesota work. A playlist is not engagement. You are a guest.

A colleague is not a soundtrack of their nation. Powwow is not the only music.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
School sport, nation sport, hockey, basketball, softball. Over-representation in a sport is not a personality. The kid may not play. Sport is not the only excellence you can see.

A physician, a software engineer, a language teacher, and a varsity hockey player can be in the same family. The group is not the person.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Oral literature first. Contemporary Native writers in this region. Language texts. This is not a people without letters.

### Named writers

Louise Erdrich (Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, Minneapolis) is world literature and Minnesota literary life — not one of the eleven, not a mash, a reminder that Native letters are not a museum. Anton Treuer’s Ojibwe-language work is Minnesota public scholarship. Nation newspapers, language curricula, and testimony at the legislature are literature of government.

You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know the record exists. Population size is not culture size.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Beadwork, quill, contemporary studio, wild rice as food and as nation, public art. You are a guest. Pay. A design is not a logo for the department.

A festival is not consultation. An artist who sells work and a chemist at a tribal environmental office are both this portrait.

sections.heading: Civil Rights Memory
sections.body:
Treaties. 1862. Boarding schools. Allotment. Termination and restoration. AIM in Minneapolis, 1968. ICWA 1978. The Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act. Haaland v. Brackeen 2023. Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women. Not “in the past.”

### The record

A DHS badge is not automatically help. The movement did not succeed so that the form is fair now. Empty follow-up cells on a tribal notice are a structural failure.

There is no U.S. Civil Rights Movement to copy onto this page as a template. The political literacy here is nation-to-nation, child welfare, land, language, and a state that still has to be made to keep its word.

sections.heading: Business and Work
sections.body:
Self-determination contracting (Public Law 93-638). Gaming as nation revenue, not a mascot. Tribal employment. Urban professionals. Trades. Teachers. Health clinicians. Scientists in tribal natural-resources departments. Attorneys in tribal courts and in this department. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Nation economies

A Heritage Month frybread lunch is not consultation. Notice goes to the nation as a government.

Shakopee Mdewakanton’s economic position is real and is not the Dakota story copied onto Upper Sioux or Lower Sioux. White Earth and Red Lake are not one economy. Name the nation. “Casino Indian” is not a type.

Native staff are not unpaid liaisons. Pay the work or do not ask for it.

sections.heading: Healthcare Encounters
sections.body:
Ask where they get care. Indian Health Service, tribal health, urban Indian health, and county clinics are not one door. Believe pain. Family and ceremony if they want them.

Refer with competence. Mandated reporting still exists. Staff are not unpaid cultural experts.

### Trust

Mistrust is historical and current. Help-seeking that becomes a child-welfare petition is a pattern families already know. Tuskegee is African American medical history — not this page. Do name this pattern: a county file that sounds like removal.

Gender match if they want it. Do not force a handshake. Inquiry under ICWA and MIFPA is not optional curiosity.

sections.heading: Diaspora and Adjacent
sections.body:
Alaska Native is a different brief. Other U.S. tribal citizens living in Minnesota are not automatically one of the eleven. First Nations from Canada are not the eleven. Urban Native is not a leftover.

### Not one Native module

Never one Native module. “Indigenous” is not a mash with Māori training slides. Open the Alaska Native brief for Alaska Native people. Open this for the eleven and for urban Native Minnesota that still belongs to a nation.

Historic African American, Somali, and Hmong are different cultural intelligences. Shared “people of color” language in a training is not shared nationhood.

sections.heading: Statistics
sections.body:
Compass Native American (ACS 2019–2023), dated: about 162,216; Twin Cities 44.8 percent, Greater Minnesota 55.2 percent; 40.1 percent age 17 or younger; 7.0 percent 65+; 3.8 percent foreign-born.

### Language, education, income

Language (age 5+): 87.9 percent English only, 12.1 percent another language, 3.2 percent English less than very well. Education (25+): 88.4 percent high school or higher, 22.5 percent bachelor’s or higher. Median household income about $58,000; 17.9 percent below poverty; 54.4 percent owner-occupied; average household size 2.54; disability 16.2 percent; without health insurance 8.5 percent.

### What the count is not

Compass cannot disaggregate by tribe. Counts disagree with enrollment, with “American Indian alone,” and with “alone or in combination.” Date the number you cite. A rate is not the person.

Child-welfare disproportionality is a gate. Health outcomes — date the controlling Minnesota Department of Health or tribal-epidemiology source. Do not invent a statewide “worst” percentage if you cannot date it.

Population size is not culture size. 162,216 is not permission to write a brochure.

sections.heading: Resources
sections.body:
Each nation’s government. Minnesota Indian Affairs Council. DHS Office of Indian Policy. Tribal-State Relations Training. ICWA and MIFPA. Haaland v. Brackeen (2023). Urban Indian organizations named on this page. Compass Native American profile — administrative, not government-to-government. A community leadership council is not a substitute for government-to-government.

### Learn on your own time

Take Tribal-State Relations Training. A Native colleague is not an unpaid tutor. Pay partners. Report back.

The Office of Equal Opportunity and Access is a discrimination door, not this page. The African American brief is not this page. Alaska Native is not this page.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Child welfare: ICWA and MIFPA. Active efforts are documented work with the family’s people, culture, and values — not a box after a removal. Kin search is not flavor. If you work that system, the nation is a government, not a culture consult.

Health and disability: IHS, tribal health, urban Indian health, county. They are not interchangeable. Believe reported pain. Olmstead still applies. Ceremony is not DHS programming.

Notices and comment: notice to nations on the same day as an eList is not consultation. Empty follow-up cells are a structural failure. Pay. Report back.

If you skip consultation because you “understand Native culture now,” this failed and it may be unlawful.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about Alaska Native peoples who live, work, study, and use services in Minnesota. Alaska Native is not one of the eleven Minnesota nations, and not a culture sticker on an Ojibwe file.

### Who this is

Iñupiaq, Yup’ik, Cup’ik, Unangax̂ (Aleut), Alutiiq / Sugpiaq, Athabascan peoples (including Gwich’in and others), Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian are distinct. Some people from those nations live in Minnesota. Sovereignty still belongs to their nations. ANCSA corporations are not the same object as Bois Forte or Lower Sioux.

Community portrait: attorneys, physicians, scientists, teachers, military families, Mayo and university students, people who work for tribally run and corporate programs, artists, and elders. Not one socioeconomic slice. Not a subsistence cartoon copied onto a St. Paul lobby.

There is no Compass cultural-community count for Alaska Native Minnesota on this page. That absence is a finding. Date a Minnesota-specific number when a controlling source exists. Do not invent a population from the eleven.

### Who this is not

This is not the eleven Minnesota nations. Filing this household under “Native” next to Leech Lake closes the meeting with a polite label. Other U.S. tribal citizens living here are not this page by default.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. Ask which nation. Always defer to this family. Population in this state may be small. Culture is not. A small Minnesota count is not permission to write a brochure.

The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Alaska Native peoples are older than the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act and older than this department. Distinct languages, territories, and legal histories.

### Named peoples

Iñupiaq of the north; Yup’ik and Cup’ik of the west; Unangax̂ of the Aleutians; Alutiiq / Sugpiaq of Kodiak and the gulf; Athabascan interior peoples; Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian of the southeast. They are not one people.

### Legal history

Russian colonial period, U.S. purchase (1867), territorial status, statehood (1959), and the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (1971) are legal history. ANCSA created regional and village corporations. Corporations are not nations by another name. Nations remain.

### What people brought

Nationhood, language, kinship, land and water relationship, subsistence as structure in home communities. What they meet in Minnesota: an English form and a checkbox that already had eleven nations on it.

History is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family.

sections.heading: Geography
sections.body:
Homelands remain in Alaska. Minnesota is where some citizens live now — Twin Cities, Rochester, military and health corridors, university towns, ordinary counties. There is not a reservation of theirs in this state.

### Name the nation

Distance to home is how the work actually runs — airfare, time zones, who can sit with an elder in Bethel or Nome while a form is in St. Paul. Nationhood is not a Minnesota ZIP code.

### Regions are not interchangeable

Southeast (Tlingit, Haida, Tsimshian) is not North Slope Iñupiaq. Yup’ik villages are not Anchorage by default. Ask.

sections.heading: Migration and Foundational Events
sections.body:
People move for school, work, military service, and health care — including Minnesota specialty care — and remain of their nations. Nationhood was not left behind in Alaska.

### Boarding schools

Boarding schools in Alaska and in the Lower 48 are part of this history. If you only know a Minnesota powwow, you will misfile this household.

### ANCSA, 1971

If the Great Migration is Black America’s foundational demographic event and 1862 is Dakota Minnesota’s, ANCSA and boarding school are literacy here. Corporations and cash settlements did not end nationhood.

### Why Minnesota

Mayo, universities, military, and ordinary jobs. Ask how they got here. Do not assume they are “from the eleven.”

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Kinship systems vary by nation. Who cares for the child may not match a nuclear English form. Ask who should be in the room.

### ICWA

ICWA still applies to Indian children as defined in federal law — including Alaska Native children. That is statute. Follow it. Still see a family. Do not copy a Leech Lake script onto the wrong nation without asking which law applies.

### Who decides

You do not decide who is Alaska Native. The nation does.

sections.heading: Minnesota
sections.body:
People live, work, and use services here. The Office of Indian Policy and the eleven are not automatic doors for Alaska Native households.

### Partners they name

Partners they name. Pay. Report back. Urban Indian organizations some people use — including the Indian Health Board of Minneapolis. Ask. Copying Leech Lake and stopping is not notice.

### Staff in the building

Staff who are Alaska Native are colleagues, not unpaid liaisons. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Count

Date a Minnesota-specific count when you have it. Pattern now. A missing cell is a finding.

sections.heading: Heart of the People
sections.body:
Nationhood first. Language, land, kinship, subsistence as structure in home communities.

### Not a copy of another page

This is not the Eleven Nations page with a different map. It is not a Somali or African American sentence because the checkbox was “other.”

### The group is not the person

Iñupiaq is not Tlingit. A scientist in Rochester and a hunter at home can be the same family.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
These concepts recur. They express differently by nation and family. They are hypotheses — not a script for the person in front of you.

### Named nations

Ask which nation. The names on this page are not flavor.

### Subsistence

Structure in home communities — and it may still sit in a Minnesota household as food, money, kinship, and seasonal travel.

### ANCSA

A legal fact, not a personality. Corporations are not nations by another name.

### Language and ceremony

Language. Ceremony as nationhood, not a module. Blood quantum and enrollment are nation business. Two-spirit people exist. Urban life in Minnesota is not assimilation by default.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing

Traditional practice and Christianity both live here — Russian Orthodox in some regions, other churches, and traditional practice.

### This family, this nation

Ceremony is not department programming. Hmong txiv neeb is not this page. Dakota lodge is not this page.

Follow this family and this nation. Clergy are the case plan when they asked.

Ask how to say it. English names and nation names may both sit on one person.

You do not decide who is Alaska Native. The nation does. A name is not a quiz.

Nation calendars and subsistence seasons in home communities. Ordinary Minnesota school calendars here.

Literacy, not a flyer.

University students, researchers, teachers, and physicians from these nations live in Minnesota. Community portrait is not a dropout cartoon. Population here is not culture size.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This page is European American cultural intelligence in Minnesota — historic cultures, not a “white people” mash. Norwegian Lutheran farm culture, German civic order, Irish Catholic St. Paul, Iron Range, Yankee New England, and later European streams are not one module. That mash is the same error we refused for Black and Asian.

### Who this is

People of color have to understand these cultures too. Dominant-culture staff have to see them as culture, not as professionalism. This is not white-versus-minority as the only frame. It is not a claim that racism is symmetrical. The record still exists.

Minnesota State Demographic Center, 2018 ACS ancestry (people could report more than one): German about 1,801,700; Norwegian 810,300; Irish 516,500; Swedish 429,800; English 290,200; Polish 248,000. Overlap is the point. Date 2018.

### Who this is not

This is not one white people. It is not a substitute for Somali, Hmong, African American, or the eleven nations. It is not a claim that racism is symmetrical.

### How to read this

Always defer to this family. Open the people brief that matches the household in front of you.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of Settler Cultures Here
sections.body:
After Indigenous nations: French; Yankee; then large German and Scandinavian streams; Irish, Slavic, and others. Homestead, railroad, church, and cooperative institutions.

### History for the meeting

A people who think they have no culture will call their form “neutral.” That is the founding problem this brief exists to name. History is literacy for the desk, including for staff of color who did not grow up inside this unmarked system.

### What people brought

Full mosaic by stream is still deepening. German, Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, Irish, Czech, Polish are separate grammars, not a race poster.

sections.heading: Geography
sections.body:
Farm counties. Iron Range. St. Paul Irish and German civic. Scandinavian towns. Later metro suburbs. Not one map.

### Homeland

These streams came from named places in Europe. They are not a blank. Name the stream.

### Minnesota

Name the stream and the town. Iron Range is not a Minneapolis suburb.

sections.heading: Migration and Foundational Events
sections.body:
Homestead and railroad. Later European streams. People leave and return.

### Foundational events

Settler presence is not empty of 1862.

### Who you meet

Do not tell a Native household this is “everyone’s immigration story.”

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Nuclear forms that feel like nature. Kin still sit in farm and church networks. “Just the parents” is already a design choice.

### Who is in the household

Ask who should be in the room. Do not treat nuclear as professional and extended as deficit.

### Who speaks

The person who talks in the lobby may not be the person who decides. Follow this room.

sections.heading: Minnesota
sections.body:
Unmarked operating system of much of this department. County desks. Church geography.

### Places

Name it. Do not mock it. Do not let it write the cap as “just being adult.”

### Partners

Church geography is real. It is not “the community.” Open the people brief that matches this household.

sections.heading: Heart — Unmarked Grammar
sections.body:
Minnesota Nice is often unmarked Scandinavian-German Protestant civic culture: conflict-avoidance, sameness-as-fairness, time and forms that feel like “just being adult.” It is not kindness as such. It can hide harm and also hold real communal obligation. Both can be true.

### In this state

When a unit says “we don’t see color, we treat everyone the same,” you are often inside this grammar. Seeing it as culture is the work. A room that treats everyone the same calls it just being decent.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
These concepts recur. They are hypotheses you still test on this family.

### Sameness-as-fairness

Identical process as the fairness story. Not a statute.

### Conflict-avoidance

Don’t make a scene. An indirect no is still a no.

### Appointment as moral

On-time as virtue. Other time grammars are not rudeness.

### Emotional restraint as professionalism

Lutheran-civic work ethic as a story about the self. Distrust of “too much” difference in public. You work with these. You do not perform a lutefisk joke as the file.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
sections.body:
Lutheran, Catholic, evangelical, Jewish religious life — related to ethnicity here and not the same object.

### Streams

Open the religion track. Do not make the pastor the case plan unless they asked.

### Practice

Church geography is operations for some households. You still keep medical and legal time.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Handshake. First names fast in some rooms, titles in others.

### Titles

Follow this room. Do not treat first-name speed as the professional standard for every household.

### This room

“Have a good one” as close is this grammar. It is not universal warmth.

sections.heading: Naming
sections.body:

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about rural Minnesota as geography and infrastructure. It is not a racial type. Rural is not code for white.

### Who this is

Farmer and miner are not the same. Somali households in Worthington, Mexican households in a dairy county, Hmong households that do live outside the metro, and the eleven nations are not afterthoughts.

Open the people brief and this place brief together when both apply. Name the town. Greater Minnesota is not one region and not one people.

A community portrait here is not a pickup-truck cartoon and not a poverty poster. Financial analysts in county buildings, scientists in plant labs, physicians in critical-access hospitals, teachers, attorneys, remote professionals, farmers, miners, plant workers, dairy workers, and small Main Street owners — all of that is Greater Minnesota. Dominant culture does not get to choose which slice is “the real rural.” People of color in these towns are not visitors in someone else’s landscape.

A St. Paul form that only works on good broadband is a gate. Print in the office still matters. A phone that works still matters. Population density is not culture size. A small town is not a thin brief.

### Who this is not

Rochester is not “rural” because it is outside the metro — it is a health city. Duluth is not a farm. Bemidji is not Worthington. This is not the European American brief and not a substitute for Somali, Mexican, Hmong, or the eleven nations.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. Always defer to this family and this county. The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture.

1862 is Dakota literacy that sits on this ground. Boarding schools sat in this geography. Farm crisis, mine closures, and hospital consolidation are later chapters of the same map. History is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech.
