An Amhara Orthodox grandmother who fasts more days than the clinic has slots, a Protestant professional, a Muslim Ethiopian household, a person who uses Amharic at work and Oromo at home, a U.S.-born student who uses English with friends and Amharic with an elder, a Tigrayan family who should not have been booked here — share a language door and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Amhara peoplehood and Amharic as a written language are older than the refugee file and older than 1974. Highland agricultural life, Ethiopian imperial history, the Orthodox Tewahedo Church, and Ge’ez as liturgical language organized a state that was not a European colony in the way the Somali and Karen files were. That fact is literacy. It is not a rank you give the family, and it is not a reason to skip language access.

### History for the meeting

Amharic became the court and then the federal working language. That is why a non-Amhara Ethiopian may speak it and still not be this people-page as a first identity. Empire’s second language in a Minnesota home is a Tuesday question: which language does this elder actually use for a legal notice?

### What people brought

1974 ended the empire. The Derg, the Red Terror, the 1980s famine, and 1991 are the foundational political events of much of the Minnesota first wave. The 2020–2022 war in Tigray is current structure for some households — Tigrayan, Amhara, Eritrean-adjacent, and others. Do not referee it in a waiver meeting.

What people brought: Amharic and fidel, Orthodox fasting and Protestant and Muslim streams, kin obligation, injera as ordinary food, honorifics, a memory of state violence. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Ethiopian” checkbox, and often one interpreter who was Somali or Oromo because the building mashed the Horn.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Amharic-speaking World
sections.body:
Homeland is not one ethnic map. Amhara region, Addis Ababa, and a country where Amharic is heard in offices far from Amhara land. Tigray, Oromia, the south, and Eritrea are adjacent geographies with different languages. Do not draw one Ethiopia on a case note.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global: Washington D.C. as a large U.S. hub, Los Angeles, Dallas, Toronto, the Gulf, Italy. Minnesota is a real community, not the U.S. capital of it. Secondary migration and church networks pulled people here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass Ethiopian is 89.4 percent Twin Cities. Minneapolis parishes (Debre Selam Medhanealem Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church among them, Seward / Minnehaha). Inner-ring suburbs. Greater Minnesota — including Worthington, where Ethiopian Orthodox life is public — is 10.6 percent of the Compass Ethiopian umbrella. Do not assume Cedar-Riverside. That hub is Somali. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Addis.

sections.heading: 1974, the Derg, Famine, and Tigray — Foundational Events
sections.body:
If 1991 is Somali Minnesota’s foundational political event, 1974 and what followed is the foundational event of much of Amharic-speaking Minnesota’s first wave.

### Foundational events

The revolution overthrew Haile Selassie. The Derg and the Red Terror killed and scattered people. The 1980s famine and resettlement brought some of the first African refugees Minnesota named as Ethiopian — MSP Magazine: Minnesota admitted 17 refugees from Ethiopia in 1982, the first African refugees in the state’s telling of that file. Others came through Sudan, Kenya, Europe. 1991 ended the Derg and opened another politics. Family reunification and later diversity streams followed.

### Who you meet

2020–2022 war in Tigray is current structure. Some Minnesota households are living it through kin, remittance, silence, or politics in the parish parking lot. Do not referee. Do not pick a side. Do not make a waiver meeting a map of the front.

The desk in 2026 also meets U.S.-born children — English with peers, still translating, still unable to get Amharic (or the actual home language) in the lobby. If you only know “Ethiopian,” you will miss the Oromo mother and the Tigrayan elder you booked wrong.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Family is larger than a nuclear English form. Elders often speak first. Godparent and kin ties, adult children in the same week as a waiver, and a grandmother who is the childcare. Compass Ethiopian average household size 3.09 — umbrella, dated, smaller than some other Compass communities, still not Mary Jones.

### Who is in the household

Who cares for the child may not match the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who speaks

Naming is already a who: given name plus father’s name, often no surname. The database that invents a last name invents a kinship the family did not file.

Ask who should be in the room. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it respect for elders. Minnesota law still stands.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Amharic-speaking History
sections.body:
Amharic-speaking Minnesota is why this page has to be as complete as Somali and Hmong — because this department will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment, and because the building has a long habit of hearing “East African” and booking Somali.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Minneapolis parishes; inner-ring suburbs; Worthington and other Greater Minnesota towns where Orthodox liturgy is public; not Cedar-Riverside as the default. Compass Ethiopian: about nine in ten in the Twin Cities.

### Partners

Partners: Orthodox parishes families name (Debre Selam Medhanealem among them); Protestant congregations; Ethiopian Community in Minnesota as historical local door; Ethiopian Community Development Council affiliates; SOS Amharic voter tools as proof the state already knew this language; CECLC as a department door — not the whole community.

Amharic-speaking staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A Timkat visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Amharic-speaking Minnesota — the heart of a people
sections.body:
To speak Amharic in Minnesota is sometimes to be Amhara, and sometimes to be a person the empire taught a second language. Both sit in this door. Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo is central for many Amhara. Protestant and Muslim Ethiopian streams are real. Intra-Ethiopian politics — Amhara, Oromo, Tigrayan — live in Minnesota parking lots. You do not pick a side.

### In this state

In this building another fact sits on top: many of these households are Black in a U.S. racial order that will file them under Somali or under historic African American and get the language, the church, and the name wrong. Shared race is not shared culture.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Language first. Confirm whether Amharic is the home language or the working language. Afaan Oromoo and Tigrinya are not dialects of Amharic.

### Orthodox fasting and calendar

Many fast days — weekly Wednesday and Friday for some, long Lenten and Advent fasts, other seasons. This is operations for appointments, blood draws, and medication with food. It is not a piety rank.

### Honorifics

Ato (Mr.), Weizero (Mrs.), Weizerit (Miss). Church titles. Elders.

### Three names

Given name, father’s name, often grandfather’s. No family surname as the database wants. Same trap as Somali. Different grammar. Do not invent a last name.

### Elders and face

Direct refusal may be costly. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### Injera, coffee ceremony, parish

Ordinary life, not a festival you attend as consultation.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
sections.body:
Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo is central for many Amhara households — one of the oldest Christian churches, Ge’ez liturgy, icons, fasting, Timkat, Meskel, Gena (January 7). Debtera and priest are church roles. They are not the case plan unless this family asked. Do not book a liturgy as DHS programming.

### Streams

Protestant and evangelical Ethiopian streams are large in the diaspora. Muslim Ethiopian streams exist — ask; book the language; do not copy Somali Islam onto this page; lunar Islamic dates if this family is Muslim.

### Practice

Fasting calendars are operations. A missed morning appointment during a fast, a medication labeled “with food,” a blood draw — ask. Noncompliance may be the calendar you never learned.

Illness meaning may sit next to holy water, vow, and parish counsel. You can hold that next to a waiver. You do not mock it. You do not skip the clinic.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Elders first. Ato, Weizero, Weizerit plus the given name until invited otherwise. Church titles for a priest. Say the name. Ask how to say it.

### Titles

Shoulder bumps and cheek kisses (often two or three) happen in some rooms among people who already know each other. A hard American handshake is not universal. Some people will shake in English-language offices. Follow this room. Do not force a hand. Do not copy Somali right-hand-across-gender rules blindly — and do not assume they do not apply. Ask the room.

### This room

Selam, tenastëllïn, English hello — follow what they offer. Do not import the Black nod as default. This is not that grammar unless this person uses it.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
Often given name plus father’s given name. The second name is not a family surname as the database wants it. Children take the father’s given name as their second name. The grandfather’s name may appear as a third. Same trap as Somali, different grammar, different people. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. That invented name becomes a gate that follows the person to Medicaid, school, and a background check.

### How to file

Women do not automatically take a husband’s name. Ask how to file. Do not “correct” a mother and child who do not share a last name as fraud until you have a reason.

Honorifics: Ato, Weizero, Weizerit. Use them. Pronounce the name. Ask. The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
Enkutatash — Ethiopian New Year, 11 September (12 September after a Gregorian leap year). Public and parish. Literacy. Not a day off the work unless they asked.

### Calendar

Timkat (Epiphany, 19 January). Meskel (Finding of the True Cross, late September). Gena — Orthodox Christmas, 7 January. Fasika — Easter, on the Orthodox calculation. Fasting seasons before these, and weekly fasts for some. Operations.

Lunar Islamic dates if this family is Muslim. Do not assume they are not.

A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “African holiday” on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Compass Ethiopian, age 25+, umbrella: about 81.5 percent high school or higher; about 24.6 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date it. It is not an Amharic-only rate. A professional class is real. So is an elder who reads fidel and not the English IEP.

### School and language

Fidel literacy is not English literacy. A parent who writes Amharic and cannot run an exception form in English is not illiterate. The English-only form is the gate.

Confirm whether Amharic is first language. An Oromo parent given an Amharic interpreter is still a closed door. Second-generation English is common. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Elders first. Shoes off in some homes. Right hand for food and for greeting in many rooms. Hospitality is a virtue — coffee, injera. Accept a little if offered. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not photograph icons, the iconostasis, or a fasting table as tourism. Do not comment on fasting as a diet.

### Time

Church time can run long. Sunday and feast-day mornings are operations. On-time for your appointment still matters. Name the conflict. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Confirm in the language they use.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Amharic. Fidel (Ge’ez-derived script). Ge’ez is liturgical, not the interview language. Compass Ethiopian umbrella: among those 5 and older, about 74.9 percent speak a language other than English; about 30.4 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date it. It is not an Amharic-only LEP rate.

### Language

An Oromo interpreter is the wrong door. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door. A Tigrinya interpreter is the wrong door unless they asked for Tigrinya. Confirm whether Amharic is first language or the empire’s second language in this home. Book what they name.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree.

Do not make an Amharic-speaking coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Intra-Ethiopian political tension in Minnesota is real — Amhara, Oromo, Tigrayan, and the Tigray war as current structure. Do not pick a side. Do not pretend the parking lot is one “Ethiopian community.” Parish and Facebook are not a case plan.

Colorism and highland/lowland hierarchy travel. You do not audit skin. You also do not delete the hierarchy to keep a training comfortable. LGBTQ Amharic-speaking Minnesotans exist. Conservative Orthodox, Protestant, and Muslim climates can mean silence. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture.

FGC is not the Amhara default story. Do not paste the Somali chapter here. If a household names it, follow law. Do not skip mandated reporting as humility. Enforcement climate changes who opens the door. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Compass Ethiopian disability 5.4 percent — umbrella, dated. Fasting interacts with diabetes medication, pregnancy advice, and lab timing. Ask. “Noncompliance” may be the fast you never put on the appointment.

### Access

There is no Amharic-specific Minnesota autism rate on this page. Do not invent one. Do not paste Somali ADDM or Hmong under-identification onto this people. Screen. Date a study when a controlling source exists.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Believe reported pain. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic “African immigrant” slide.

Holy water, vow, and parish counsel can sit next to biomedicine. If they name a healer or a priest, listen. Do not make them the case plan unless they asked.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Amharic-speaking Minnesotans exist. Conservative Orthodox, Protestant, and Muslim climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Amharic life.

### This person

You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies.

So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Orthodox white netela or gabi in church is not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the shawl.”

### Dress

Hair, covering, and modest dress vary by Orthodox, Protestant, Muslim, and secular practice. Do not touch. This is not the CROWN Act chapter and not the Somali hijab chapter.

Follow this person. Gender match if she wants it.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Orthodox chant in Ge’ez, kebero drums, eskista as dance, Protestant worship music, diaspora pop.

### Variation

Liturgy is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement.

A Timkat procession is public; you are a guest.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Distance running is a public image of Ethiopia. It is not a personality and not a health history.

### Not the whole person

Soccer and ordinary school sport are real in the second generation. Sport clubs are not language access and not a case plan.

Do not assume the kid runs.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Ge’ez and Amharic written tradition is old — older than the refugee file. Fidel made a public possible. Newspapers, church texts, diaspora writers, second-generation English.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters.

The English form may still be unreadable to the parent who reads fidel.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Orthodox iconography, textile, church architecture, injera as ordinary table not a Heritage Month sample. Parish as public art for some.

### Guest

Guest. A Timkat procession is not consultation. A museum visit is not a case plan.

Do not put an icon on a unit display.

sections.heading: Conflict, War, and the State
sections.body:
Imperial history, 1974, the Red Terror, the Derg, the 1980s famine, 1991, and the 2020–2022 Tigray war as current structure — that is the political file. Intra-Ethiopian politics in Minnesota are not folklore.

### The badge

A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not referee the Tigray war in a waiver meeting. Do not pick a side.

Do not ask anyone to narrate killing for your professional development. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a faction score.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Compass Ethiopian, dated umbrella: median household about $57,106; poverty 13.0 percent; renter 65.3 percent. Restaurants, parking, care work, professional class, public employment. Pattern, not a personality.

### Work

Amharic-speaking staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Staff

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Wrong language door — Somali, Oromo, Tigrinya when they asked for Amharic, or Amharic when the home language is not. Three-name form. Fasting vs appointment. Who is in the room. Intra-community tension. Enforcement climate.

### Language

Confirm Amharic is the home language. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

If they name a priest, listen. Mandated reporting still exists.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not Oromo as a synonym. Not Tigrayan as a synonym. Not Somali. Not Eritrean by default — Tigrinya and Arabic and a different state. Not Kenyan. Not historic African American. Not “East African interpreter.”

### Adjacent doors

Compass Ethiopian is the umbrella. This page is the Amharic door. If the household is Oromo, open Oromo. If Tigrayan, Tigrinya. If Somali — including Ethiopia-born Somali ancestry — Somali Minnesota.

Some households are mixed. Ask this household. Never one Ethiopian module.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Ethiopian cultural community (umbrella): 40,324; Twin Cities 89.4%; Greater Minnesota 10.6%; age 17 or younger 43.5%; 65+ 3.6%; foreign-born 61.7%; language other than English (age 5+) 74.9%; English less than “very well” 30.4%; high school or higher (25+) 81.5%; bachelor’s or higher 24.6%; median household income about $57,106 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 13.0%; renter-occupied 65.3%; owner-occupied 34.7%; average household size 3.09; disability 5.4%.

### Counts

Respondents born in Ethiopia who list Somali ancestry are counted Somali, not Ethiopian. Census recodes some Oromo write-ins as Ethiopian. This is not an Amharic speaker count. Do not invent one.

### What the count is not

Minnesota Secretary of State voter materials include Amharic — operations evidence that the language is in the state, not a population.

Date the number. A young age structure is not a personality. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass Ethiopian profile (ACS 2019–2023). Compass cultural-communities methodology (Oromo recode; Somali ancestry carved out). CLAS fifteen interpreter cards: Amharic. Minnesota Secretary of State Amharic voter tools. Orthodox parishes families name, including Debre Selam Medhanealem. Ethiopian Community in Minnesota as historical local door. Ethiopian Community Development Council affiliates. Pay. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Public doors

CECLC is a door, not the whole community. Learn on your own time. Do not make an Amharic-speaking colleague your unpaid tutor.

### Learn on your own time

Report back. Guest.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled Ethiopian, Somali, or Oromo who is not Amharic as this household speaks it is a closed door. Confirm whether Amharic is first language or the empire’s second language in this home. If Oromo, book Afaan Oromoo. If Tigrayan, book Tigrinya. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: given name plus father’s name. The database that invents a last name is a gate that follows the person. Same trap as Somali. Different people.

Fasting: Wednesday, Friday, Lent, Advent, other seasons for many Orthodox households. Medication with food, labs, morning appointments. Ask. “No-show” may be the feast you scheduled against.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. SOS already prints Amharic for voters — the packet can too.

Workforce: Amharic-speaking staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that heard “East African” and booked Somali.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is a language door, not a people. “French-speaking Minnesota” names a CLAS fifteen line and a set of households who may use French at school, at the clinic, or with the state — and who often use another language at home. Ask which French, and whether another language is actually the home language.

### Who this is

Streams that are not interchangeable: Haiti, where Kreyòl (Haitian Creole) is often the home language and French the school or official language; West and Central Africa, where Wolof, Bambara, Lingala, Kinyarwanda, and many others may be home and French the colonial/school language; France, Belgium, Quebec, and other European or North American streams — smaller in Minnesota services, real; some Somali and other Horn households with French from Djibouti or camps — not the default.

### Who this is not

This is not historic African American CI with a different flag. It is not Somali. It is not one Africa. It is not France. Do not assume Africa. Do not assume France. Do not assume Haiti. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### How to read this

There is no Minnesota Compass cultural-community row for “French” or “Francophone.” Do not invent a census. Star Tribune (July 31, 2025): among people in Minnesota who speak a language other than English at home, French is among the languages — with German, Chinese, Russian, and Arabic — each representing about 2 percent of that group. Date it. That is a language share. It is not a Haitian count, not a Senegalese count, not a Québécois count.

The diversity inside the door is the point. A Kreyòl-speaking mother, a Lingala-speaking father from Kinshasa who uses French with the school, a Dakar household that wants Wolof, a Quebecois professional, a French national on a campus, a Djiboutian elder who has French from a camp — do not share a Tuesday.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins — several peoples, one colonial language
sections.body:
Haitian peoplehood is not an African checkbox and not a French checkbox. The Haitian Revolution reached independence on January 1, 1804 — the first Black republic in the hemisphere. U.S. occupation (1915–1934), dictatorships, the 2010 earthquake, and later TPS designations are Haitian history. Kreyòl is the home language of the people. French was the colonial and school language. Book Kreyòl if that is the home language.

### History for the meeting

West and Central Africa are many nations and many peoples under a French school language left by colonization: Senegal, Mali, Guinea, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Congo-Brazzaville, francophone Rwanda and Burundi, and others. Wolof, Bambara, Lingala, Kinyarwanda, Fulani, and more may be what the grandmother actually speaks. An “African French” interpreter can still be the wrong door.

### What people brought

France, Belgium, Switzerland, and Quebec are European and North American streams. They are smaller in Minnesota human services. They are real. Do not assume Africa when the household is Paris. Do not assume Paris when the household is Port-au-Prince or Yaoundé.

Some Somali and other Horn households have French from Djibouti, from camps, or from a third country. That is not the default for Somali Minnesota. Open Somali for Somali. Ask about French if they name it.

sections.heading: The Geography of French as a Door
sections.body:
Haiti is Caribbean. Dakar, Bamako, Abidjan, Yaoundé, Kinshasa, Brazzaville, Kigali, Bujumbura are African cities with different languages under the French door. Paris, Brussels, Montreal are not those cities.

### Homeland

Minnesota is a present. Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota both. Do not assume Minneapolis. Plant towns, student neighborhoods, and inner-ring suburbs can all hold a household on this door.

### Minnesota

There is no Compass map for this umbrella. Date any town-level school-language count when a professional has it. Pattern now: people are here. Do not invent a county number.

sections.heading: 1804, Occupation, Earthquake, Colonies, and TPS — Foundational Events
sections.body:
Haiti: 1804 is peoplehood. The U.S. occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934. The January 12, 2010 earthquake killed on a scale this building should not turn into a speech. Temporary Protected Status for Haiti was first designated after that earthquake and has been extended, terminated, and redesignated in later years — including after the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse and another earthquake. Date the designation you mean. Do not invent this person’s status. Do not collect status you do not need.

### Foundational events

West and Central African migration into Minnesota includes students, skilled workers, family, and people displaced by conflict. French is often the language a school left them, not the language of the kitchen. Colonial borders and later wars are literacy. They are not a news-clip briefing you give the family.

### Who you meet

Euro-French, Belgian, and Quebec streams arrive as professionals, students, and family. Smaller in the service lobby, real. Do not run a refugee script on a Lyon household. Do not run a Paris script on a Cap-Haïtien household.

If you only know “French,” you will miss Kreyòl, miss Lingala, and mash a people.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Extended household is common in many Haitian and West/Central African streams. Godparents, church sisters, mosque kin, and cousins who are “auntie” on Tuesday may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who is in the household

Euro-French nuclear grammar is not the default for this door. Do not import it.

### Who speaks

Who cares for the child, who holds the lease, and who can sign may not be the same adult. Mixed-status households exist in Haitian and some African streams. Do not collect status you do not need.

Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture. Do not turn a family argument into a national personality.

sections.heading: Minnesota and This Language Door
sections.body:
This department will meet these households on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, TPS-adjacent fear, and employment. Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota. Rural is not an afterthought when the plant or the college is the draw.

### Places

Churches (Catholic and Protestant) and mosques are often the actual information channel. Parish and mosque are not “the community.” They are a door if this family names them.

### Partners

Alliance Française and campus French clubs are Euro-French civic and student doors. They are not the service partner for a Haitian or Senegalese household unless that household names them. Do not BCC a conversation group and call it consultation.

Do not make Haitian, Senegalese, Congolese, or Cameroonian staff the interpreter pool or “the African voice.”

sections.heading: A language door, not a people mash
sections.body:
To be filed under French in Minnesota is often to be asked whether you are from France, or from Africa, as if those were two rooms and Haiti were in one of them.

### In this state

Anti-Blackness in this state hits Haitian and African francophone people in the lobby, the clinic, and the traffic stop. That is not a reason to open historic African American CI and stop. Open African American for a Great Migration household. Open this for a Haitian or Senegalese household. Open Somali for Somali. Shared race in the United States is not shared culture. Shared French class in a colonial school is not shared culture.

Colorism sits inside some Haitian and West African families and inside Minnesota’s racial order. You do not lecture it. You do not pretend it is absent.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Home language is the first grammar. French may be school. Kreyòl, Lingala, Wolof, Bambara, or Kinyarwanda may be home. Book home.

### One Francophone client is a mash

Haiti is not Senegal. DRC is not Cameroon. Quebec is not Port-au-Prince.

### Colorism and anti-Blackness

Both can be in the room. Neither is a personality.

### Church or mosque as channel

Not the case plan unless they asked.

### TPS and enforcement climate

People skip clinic and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance.

### Respect and titles in many streams

Do not force first-name familiarity on an elder.

sections.heading: Religion
sections.body:
Catholic Christianity is large in Haiti and in parts of West and Central Africa and in Euro-French streams. Protestant and evangelical churches are ordinary too. Islam is ordinary in much of West Africa and present in some Haitian households. None is real.

### Streams

Vodou is a Haitian religious fact in some households. Do not sensationalize it. Do not treat it as horror-film content, as witchcraft for the file, or as the “real” Haiti. Do not make a Vodou priest the case plan unless this family asked. The same rule for a Catholic priest or an imam.

### Practice

Do not assume a mosque because the passport is West African. Do not assume a cathedral because the language is French.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
French vous vs tu is a formality system some Euro-French and African school-French speakers use. Kreyòl greetings are not that system. Wolof and Lingala greetings are not that system. Follow this room.

### Titles

Elders and titles in many Haitian and African streams. Handshake in many professional rooms. Do not force a hug.

### This room

Do not import a Paris rule onto a Haitian elder. Do not import a Port-au-Prince manner onto a Lille professional. Do not import the Black nod or Somali right-hand rules unless this person is on those pages.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
French-style given name plus family name appears in some streams. Haitian naming may not match first-middle-last. West African naming may include a day name, a Muslim name, a family name, or a French school name that is not what the grandmother uses. Ask how to say it. Ask how to file it.

### How to file

Do not invent a last name. Do not “correct” Kreyòl or Wolof spelling to Paris French. Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as fraud by default.

A child may have a different school name than the name on the birth record. Ask. Do not humiliate.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
January 1 — Haitian Independence Day, 1804. Literacy. Not a day off the work unless this family names it. Not Bastille Day.

### Calendar

January 12, 2010 — Haiti earthquake. TPS history starts here for many families. Literacy. Not a speech.

West African independence dates vary by country (1960 is a cluster, not a single day). Catholic calendars, Ramadan and Eid in Muslim households, and national days this family names — ask. Do not put Bastille Day (July 14) on a Haitian or Senegalese case note.

A calendar click is not community engagement.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
French as a school or official language does not mean French is the home language, and does not mean the parent can run an English IEP. Literacy in any language of the form is not guaranteed. Interrupted schooling in Haiti after 2010, or in a conflict region, is structure.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Kreyòl, Wolof, or Lingala and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only form is the gate. So is a French form when the home language is Kreyòl.

Second-generation English is common. CLAS still says do not use minors as interpreters. Book the home language.

Do not invent a Minnesota Francophone attainment rate. Compass has no such row.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Titles and elders in many Haitian and African streams. Hospitality is a virtue in many rooms. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not assume a French-restaurant manner — wine, first names after one meeting, cheek kisses — is the rule in this living room. Do not assume the absence of that manner is “less educated.”

### Time

Shoes, food, and Sunday church or Friday mosque will vary. Ask. On-time for appointments is a professional default for some and a bus-and-shift problem for others.

Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Ask which language is actually home. Book that language.

### Language

Kreyòl is not French. A French interpreter for a Kreyòl household is a closed door. Lingala is not French. Wolof is not French. Bambara is not French. Kinyarwanda is not French. An interpreter billed as “African French” can still be the wrong country, the wrong register, and the wrong language.

French itself is not one French. Haitian school French, Dakar French, Kinshasa French, and Paris French differ in accent and vocabulary. Mutual understanding is often possible and not guaranteed. Ask.

Star Tribune (July 31, 2025): French is about 2 percent of the non-English-at-home group in Minnesota, listed with German, Chinese, Russian, and Arabic. Date it. That share does not tell you which French, or whether French is home.

A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Do not make a Francophone coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Anti-Blackness in Minnesota hits Haitian and African francophone people. Traffic stops, clinic dismissal, and “where are you really from” are structure. Do not fold this household into historic African American CI because both are Black — and do not pretend anti-Blackness is absent because the passport is Haitian or Senegalese.

Colorism inside families and in the U.S. racial order is real. You do not lecture it. You do not skip it when it is the harm in the room.

LGBTQ Haitian and African francophone Minnesotans exist. Enforcement and TPS climate is current structure. People skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

One Francophone client is how treating everyone the same hides difference. Haiti is not Africa. Africa is not France. France is not Haiti.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Language is the first health gate. A French consent form for a Kreyòl speaker is not consent. A smile is not consent.

### Access

Trauma and displacement in some Haitian and African streams are real. Do not invent a Minnesota Francophone PTSD rate. Do not skip screening. Do not make earthquake or war a personality.

Believe reported pain. Anti-Blackness in U.S. medicine is documented. Do not mash Tuskegee onto a Port-au-Prince or Dakar history; do not pretend the clinic is neutral.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. If they name a healer, a priest, or an imam, listen. Do not make that person the case plan unless they asked.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Haitian, African francophone, and Euro-French Minnesotans exist. Conservative church, mosque, and family climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private home-language life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat Haiti or “Africa” as a family-values exhibit.

Do not assume a Paris household is affirming. Do not assume a Port-au-Prince household is not. Ask this person.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Hair is political for many Black francophone people in this state. Natural hair, braids, locs, wraps, wigs — follow this person. Minnesota’s CROWN Act still applies. Do not touch. Do not ask to “see it out.” Do not treat a headwrap as a costume.

### Dress

Euro-French dress codes are not the rule on this door. Do not police “professional” hair on Haitian or African staff.

Festival dress is public on some dates and not a daily uniform. Do not ask if they “still wear traditional clothes.”

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Kompa and rara in Haitian public life; mbalax in Senegalese streams; Congolese rumba and ndombolo; church music; French pop. Not one soundtrack. Not a festival booth.

### Variation

A playlist is not engagement. Do not ask a client or a staff person to perform.

Sunday choir is operations for some Baptist and Catholic households. It is not consultation.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Soccer is public in many Haitian and African francophone communities. Ordinary school sport is ordinary for the second generation. Neither is language access.

### Not the whole person

Do not use a national-team jersey as a case plan. Sport clubs are not a substitute for an interpreter or a notice.

A Saturday league in a southern town is not consultation. Book the home language for the parent who is in the stands and cannot run the IEP.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Haitian literature in Kreyòl and French, Senegalese and Congolese and Cameroonian writing, and the French canon are not one shelf. Kreyòl literature is literature. Oral tradition is not the absence of letters.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do not need to quote Césaire, Chauvet, or a Paris syllabus. You need to know this door is not a people without letters, and not one people.

Do not put a proverb on a brochure and call it CLAS.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Haitian painting, sequined flags, West and Central African cloth and carving, Euro-French museum culture — not interchangeable. Do not mash them onto a generic “African art” Heritage Month table.

### Guest

Guest. Public festivals are not consultation. Do not extract a staff person’s child as entertainment.

Alliance Française gallery nights are a Euro-French civic door. They are not the service partner for a Haitian or Senegalese household unless that household names them.

sections.heading: Conflict, the State, and This Climate
sections.body:
1804 is Haitian peoplehood. U.S. occupation, dictatorship, 2010, and TPS are U.S. and Haitian state history in the same file. Colonial borders and wars in West and Central Africa produced displacement and a school language. You do not invent a briefing from a news clip.

### The badge

Enforcement climate now — TPS uncertainty, raids in the news, a relative who can be moved — changes who opens the door. A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

Do not use 1804 or 2010 as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate an earthquake or a war for your professional development.

sections.heading: Work, Business, and Government
sections.body:
Service, care work, plants in Greater Minnesota, professional class, students, small business. Do not invent a Minnesota Francophone occupational census. Compass has no such row. Pattern: people work here.

### Work

Haitian, Senegalese, Congolese, Cameroonian, and other African staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not “the African community.” Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Staff

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Home language vs school French. Kreyòl. Lingala. Wolof. Who is in the room. Gender. TPS climate. Anti-Blackness in the clinic. A priest, an imam, or Vodou in the story.

### Language

Confirm the home language. Offer gender match. Believe reported pain. Do not collect status. Do not make staff the interpreter. Mandated reporting still exists.

### The meeting

A French consent form for a Kreyòl speaker is not consent. A smile is not consent. Name who the form was built for.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not historic African American. Not Somali. Not Oromo. Not Liberian. Not Nigerian. Not one Africa. Not France as default. Open those CIs for those households.

### Adjacent doors

Haitian, Senegalese, Malian, Guinean, Ivorian, Cameroonian, Congolese, Rwandan, Burundian, and Québécois households are not interchangeable. Some Somali households have French from Djibouti or camps — not the default. Ask this household.

Never one Black module. Never one Francophone client.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated — and what you may not invent
sections.body:
There is no Minnesota Compass cultural-community row for French, Haitian, Senegalese, or “Francophone.” Do not invent a census. Do not borrow Compass African American, Somali, or Kenyan counts and file them here.

### Counts

Star Tribune, July 31, 2025, on languages spoken at home in Minnesota: among people who speak a language other than English at home, German, French, Chinese, Russian, and Arabic each represent about 2 percent of that group. Date it. That is a language share. It does not tell you home language vs school language. It does not disaggregate Kreyòl. Kreyòl may be coded elsewhere or missed. Name the gap.

### What the count is not

School-language and interpreter-request data in a county are a pattern when you have them. Date them. A rate you do not have is not a rate you may put on this page.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Star Tribune, July 31, 2025, languages spoken at home. CLAS fifteen: French. Book Kreyòl when Kreyòl is home. Book Lingala, Wolof, Bambara, or Kinyarwanda when that is home. A French interpreter can still be the wrong door.

### Public doors

Haitian, West African, and Central African associations this person names. Churches and mosques this person names. Alliance Française is a Euro-French civic door — use it if they name it, not as the default partner.

### Learn on your own time

CECLC is a door, not the whole. Learn on your own time. Do not make a Haitian or Senegalese colleague your unpaid tutor. Pay partners. Report back.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: a French interpreter for a Kreyòl household is a closed door. A French interpreter for a Lingala or Wolof household can be a closed door. “African French” is not a dialect you may invent. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: the database that invents a last name or “corrects” Kreyòl spelling to Paris French is a gate.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without the home language are not culturally neutral. An English IEP is a gate. A French packet when home is Kreyòl is a gate.

One Francophone client: Haiti is not Africa. Africa is not France. France is not Haiti. Folding a Haitian household into historic African American CI because both are Black is a closed gate with a polite label. Open the right page.

Enforcement and TPS climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how these households were reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Workforce: Haitian and African francophone staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never asked which French, or whether French was home at all.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about Burmese Minnesota as a people-page and as a warning about an umbrella. CLAS fifteen interpreter cards say Burmese. Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) says Burmese 17,123. Both are operations and a U.S. administrative name. They are not a people.

### Who this is

Not Karen as a synonym. Not Chin as a synonym. Not Kachin, not Mon, not Rohingya, not “Asian.” Compass Burmese can include Bamar — the majority people of Myanmar, often called Burman — and may overlap or sit beside Chin, Kachin, Rohingya, Mon, Karen. Compass methodology: the Census recodes some people who write Karen into Burmese, with nothing left to show the original response. Ask the people. If the household is Karen, open Karen Minnesota and put S’gaw or Pwo on the line. If Chin, book Chin — Hakha, Falam, or the variety they name. If Rohingya, Rohingya or Bengali may be the language. Burmese is not the default.

### Who this is not

Compass, dated: Twin Cities 79.9 percent, Greater Minnesota 20.1 percent. Age 17 or younger 41.5 percent; 65+ 4.2 percent. Foreign-born 67.1 percent. Language other than English (age 5+) 89.6 percent. English less than “very well” 67.0 percent — a severe language gate. High school or higher among 25+ 32.8 percent; bachelor’s or higher 11.8 percent. Median household about $75,513. Poverty 29.6 percent. Owner-occupied 59.0 percent. Average household size 4.99. Disability 12.9 percent. Date Compass. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside the umbrella is the point. A Bamar Buddhist elder who reads Myanmar script, a Hakha Chin Christian plant worker in Worthington, a S’gaw Karen household that should have opened the Karen page, a Rohingya family who should not have been booked Burmese, a U.S.-born teenager who uses English with friends and still translates a 67-percent-LEP parent — share a country checkbox and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Bamar peoplehood on the Irrawaddy is older than the British and older than the junta. Theravada Buddhism, Burmese as a tonal language with its own script, wet-rice agriculture, and a sequence of kingdoms organized a majority that is not the whole country. Chin, Kachin, Karen, Karenni, Mon, Rakhine, Rohingya, Shan, and others are peoples, not dialects. The country checkbox that says Burma or Myanmar is already a mash.

### History for the meeting

British colonial rule, independence in 1948, and decades of military government produced the file this desk meets. 1988. 2007. 2017 in Rakhine. 2021 coup — current structure. Camps in Thailand and Bangladesh are not a personality. They are years of interrupted school, interrupted care, and a kinship the form cannot see.

### What people brought

What people brought: language (maybe Burmese, maybe not), church or monastery or mosque, large household, farming and plant skill, a memory of being hunted by a state. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled Burmese for a household that is Chin or Karen.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Burmese World
sections.body:
Homeland is Myanmar — Yangon, Mandalay, the Delta, the hills, Chin State, Kachin State, Kayin, Rakhine. Do not draw one pagoda on a case note. Camps in Thailand (Mae La and others) and in Bangladesh (Cox’s Bazar and others) are origin-of-arrival for many Minnesota families. Years. Not a layover.

### Homeland

The U.S. map is not only Minnesota: Indiana, New York, Texas, California, and others hold Burma-origin communities. Minnesota is a real resettlement and secondary-migration state, including Greater Minnesota.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass Burmese 79.9 percent Twin Cities, 20.1 percent Greater Minnesota. Name the town. Worthington, Albert Lea, Austin, Marshall, and Willmar are a Karen/Burmese pattern in public telling (MSP Magazine on Minnesota’s refugee history names those towns for Karen). Do not assume St. Paul. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Yangon. A Worthington household is not a Minneapolis default.

sections.heading: Military Rule, Camps, 2017, 2021 — Foundational Events
sections.body:
If 1975 is Hmong Minnesota and 1991 is Somali Minnesota, military rule, the camps, and the later coups are the foundational events of Burma-origin Minnesota. They are not one event and not one people.

### Foundational events

MSP Magazine’s state refugee timeline: refugees from Burma arrive in Minnesota in 1993, most of them named as Karen in that telling. Later waves include Chin, Bamar, and others. 2017 Rohingya atrocities — mass killing, rape, and expulsion, named as genocide by the United States in 2022 — produced a specific flight. 2021 military coup is current structure: kin still there, remittance, silence, status anxiety here.

### Who you meet

Camps in Thailand and Bangladesh shaped literacy, time, and who counts as family. U.S. resettlement scattered people; secondary migration and church networks pulled some to Minnesota, including plant towns.

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children and a parent facing a 67 percent LEP gate. If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the 18-year-old and still fail the form for the elder. Do not ask a Rohingya survivor to narrate the village for your chart.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Households are large. Compass average household size 4.99. Married couples with children under 18 are 46.5 percent of households. Elders, in-laws, camp-made kin, adult children. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox.

### Who is in the household

Camp years shape who is kin. A cousin who is not a cousin on the English form. A missing father. A household that formed in Mae La or Cox’s Bazar. Ask who is in the room. Do not reconstruct a family tree as icebreaker.

### Who speaks

Women’s labor — plant, care, second-generation school — sits next to a household in which an elder may still be named as head. Both can be true.

Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture. Minnesota law still stands. A nuclear two-parent English form already has a who. It was built for a different household.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Burmese History
sections.body:
Minnesota holds a Burma-origin community large enough for Compass to profile it — 17,123 on the ACS 2019–2023 umbrella — and mixed enough that the profile is a gate if you treat it as one people. This department will meet these households on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment, in St. Paul and in Worthington.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; Roseville as a Karen Organization of Minnesota address (a Karen door); Greater Minnesota plant towns — Worthington, Albert Lea, Austin, Marshall, Willmar among those named in public Karen/Burmese telling. Compass: about one in five outside the Twin Cities. Name the town. Do not assume St. Paul.

### Partners

Partners: Karen Organization of Minnesota is a Karen door — not automatically this page. Burmese, Chin, and Rohingya groups and the churches, monasteries, and mosques families name. Pay the partner this household names. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community.

Burmese or Karen staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A New Year visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Burmese Minnesota — the heart of a people
sections.body:
There is not one heart under this umbrella. Bamar Theravada life, Chin Christian hill life, Karen Baptist or Buddhist life, Rohingya Muslim life — these are peoples. The U.S. file that recodes Karen as Burmese is how a census becomes a closed door.

### In this state

In Minnesota it sits inside another fact: Asian in a checkbox that also holds Hmong, Chinese, Indian, and Korean histories they do not share; camp years; Greater Minnesota isolation for some; a language gate at 67 percent LEP.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Ask who is actually in the room.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Who is in the room. Bamar, Chin, Karen, Rohingya, Mon, Kachin. Ask. The country name is not the answer.

### Language

Burmese is tonal with Myanmar script. Hakha, Falam, S’gaw, Pwo, Rohingya/Bengali are not Burmese. 67 percent LEP is the gate. Literacy in any script is not guaranteed.

### Church, monastery, mosque

Information channel for some. Not the case plan unless they asked. Sunday and moon days are operations.

### Camp time

Interrupted school, interrupted care, kin the form cannot see. 67 percent less than high school among 25+ is structure.

### Large household

4.99. Ask who should hear.

### Face and quiet endurance

A smile can be misread as agreement. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
sections.body:
Theravada Buddhist majority among Bamar — monastery, moon days (Uposatha), Thingyan, offerings. A monk is not the case plan unless this family asked. Do not book a monastery as DHS programming.

### Streams

Christian majority among many Chin and Karen streams in Minnesota — Baptist and other Protestant, some Catholic. Church is often the information channel and the English class and the ride. Sunday is operations. Church is not “the community” and not automatically the Karen Organization.

### Practice

Muslim Rohingya. Mosque, Ramadan, halal. Do not copy Somali Islam blindly; do not assume Burmese is the language. Ask.

Do not assume pagoda. Do not assume Baptist. Illness meaning may sit next to blessing, vow, or monastery counsel. You can hold that next to a clinic. You do not mock it. You do not skip the waiver.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Elders first. A slight bow or nod with an older person is safer than a hard handshake you assume is universal. Mingalaba is a common Burmese greeting. English hello is ordinary in many rooms and in the second generation. Chin and Karen greetings are not Burmese. Follow this room.

### Titles

Say the name. Ask how to say it. Do not force a hand. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. Do not import Somali right-hand rules or Hmong nyob zoo onto this page unless this person uses them.

### This room

Do not open with the junta. Do not open with “I have a Karen friend” if this household is not Karen.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
Myanmar Bamar naming often has no family surname as the database wants. Personal names may be one, two, or more syllables. Honorifics U (for a man) and Daw (for a woman) in some rooms — titles, not first names. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. That invented name becomes a gate.

### How to file

Chin and Karen naming differ — clan, baptismal, and English names exist in those streams. Rohingya naming may follow a different Muslim pattern. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it.

Do not “correct” a mother and child who do not share a last name as a fraud signal until you have a reason. The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
Thingyan — Burmese New Year, mid-April — for many Bamar Buddhist households. Water festival in the homeland; quieter in Minnesota. Literacy. Not automatically this Chin or Karen family’s day.

### Calendar

Buddhist moon days are operations for some. Sunday is operations for many Chin and Karen churches. Karen New Year is a Karen page — do not steal it as a Burmese holiday. Christmas and Easter for Christian streams. Lunar Islamic dates if this family is Rohingya or otherwise Muslim.

A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note. Ask which calendar this family uses.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Compass Burmese, age 25+: high school or higher 32.8 percent; bachelor’s or higher 11.8 percent; less than high school 67.2 percent. Date it. Camp years and interrupted schooling are structure, not a personality and not a refusal to value school.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Burmese, Hakha, or S’gaw and limited English is not illiterate. Literacy in Burmese script is not guaranteed even when Burmese is the spoken language. The English-only IEP is the gate. So is an interpreter in the wrong language.

Second-generation children are in English-dominant schools, including Greater Minnesota. The form still has to reach the parent. 41.5 percent of the Compass umbrella is 17 or younger. That is a school-and-waiver fact, not a vibe.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Shoes off in many homes, monasteries, and some churches. Elders first. Head is high; feet are low — do not point feet at an altar, a monk, or a person if you are in a Buddhist household. Do not touch a child’s head as friendliness.

### In the home

Hospitality is a virtue. Accept a little food if offered. You still keep medical and legal time.

### Time

Quiet endurance can be misread as agreement. A smile is not consent to the plan. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

On-time for appointments. Plant shifts, multi-household logistics, and Greater Minnesota distance are real. Name the conflict. Do not punish a no-show you built in English only.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Burmese (Myanmar language) is tonal and written in its own script. Confirm that this is the language. Compass: among those 5 and older, 89.6 percent speak a language other than English; 67.0 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date it. That is a severe language gate.

### Language

A “Burmese interpreter” for a Hakha Chin household is a closed door. Same for Falam, S’gaw, Pwo, Rohingya, Bengali. Put the language on the request. Literacy of the spoken language is not literacy of the form. Many camp-schooled adults do not read the script you assumed.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent.

Do not make a Burmese, Chin, or Karen coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Camp years and interrupted schooling: 67.2 percent less than high school among 25+ is structure. Do not write it as laziness or as “they don’t value education.”

Rohingya genocide is a fact. The United States determined in 2022 that the 2017 atrocities were genocide. Do not platform denial in a lobby. Do not book Burmese by default for a Rohingya household. LGBTQ people exist in every stream under this umbrella. Conservative church, monastery, and mosque climates can mean silence. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture.

Greater Minnesota isolation is real — plant town, few interpreters, English IEP, a notice that never left a St. Paul eList. Name the town. Do not file this household under Karen if they are not Karen. Do not file them under Hmong. Do not file them under Asian.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Compass Burmese: disability 12.9 percent; among under-65, 10.0 percent; uninsured 6.2 percent. Date it. Camp and interrupted-care histories — hepatitis, anemia, dental, immunization gaps — are patterns in refugee clinical literacy nationally. This page does not invent a Minnesota clinic rate. Date a local figure when a controlling source exists.

### Access

67 percent LEP is a health gate now. Literacy of the consent form is a health gate. A Burmese-script form for a person who does not read it is still a closed door.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Believe reported pain. Do not skip developmental screening. Do not mash this page with Hmong late autism identification or Somali ADDM. Those are other intelligences.

If they name a monk, a pastor, or a healer, listen. Do not make them the case plan unless they asked.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Burmese, Chin, Karen, and Rohingya Minnesotans exist. Conservative church, monastery, and mosque climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private home-language life.

### This person

You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies.

So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a family-values exhibit.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Longyi and thanaka among some Bamar — not a daily uniform in a Worthington plant. Karen and Chin traditional dress is public at New Year, not a clinic outfit. Muslim covering among some Rohingya. Second generation looks like Minnesota.

### Dress

Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch hair or thanaka. Do not mash with Hmong New Year dress or Somali hijab.

Follow this person. Gender match if she wants it.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Church hymn in many Chin and Karen streams. Buddhist ritual sound. Saung and classical Burmese as homeland art. Diaspora pop.

### Variation

Funeral, monastery, and church are not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement.

A choir is not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Soccer, volleyball, chinlone as a homeland image, ordinary school sport in the second generation. Greater Minnesota plant-town leagues exist.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are not language access and not a case plan.

Do not assume the kid plays.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Burmese script and a written public are old. Oral literature in Chin, Karen, and Rohingya streams. Camp years interrupted schooling. Second-generation English.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters — and that literacy of the English form, and of Burmese script, is not guaranteed.

The form has to match the person, not the country checkbox.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Thanaka, textile, monastery carving, church banner. Karen weaving is a Karen page — do not steal it as Burmese souvenir, and do not mash it with Hmong paj ntaub.

### Guest

Guest. A New Year is not consultation. A display table is not a case plan.

Do not put a longyi on a Heritage Month booth.

sections.heading: Conflict, War, and the State
sections.body:
British colonial rule, independence, military government, 1988, 2007, the 2017 Rohingya atrocities, and the 2021 coup as current structure — that is the political file. Camps in Thailand and Bangladesh. A United States that resettled people into plant towns and then sent English PDFs.

### The badge

Rohingya genocide is a fact. Do not platform denial. Do not ask a survivor to narrate the village for your professional development.

A DHS badge is not automatically help. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a risk score.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Compass Burmese, dated: median household about $75,513; poverty 29.6 percent; owner-occupied 59.0 percent; about 69.2 percent of working-age adults employed (18–64). Food processing and other Greater Minnesota work for many Burma-origin households. Professional second generation. Public employment.

### Work

Staff from this umbrella are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Plant shifts are operations for appointments.

### Staff

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision. A notice that never left St. Paul does not reach Worthington.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Who is actually in the room. 67 percent LEP. Literacy of the form. Greater Minnesota clinic with no interpreter on site. Church vs monastery vs mosque. Camp health history. Rohingya language not Burmese by default.

### Language

Confirm people and language. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

Believe reported pain. Mandated reporting still exists.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not Karen as a synonym — open Karen Minnesota for Karen; put S’gaw or Pwo on the line. Not Chin as a synonym — book Hakha, Falam, or the variety they name. Not Hmong. Not Vietnamese. Not Chinese. Not Thai as the camp country. Not “Asian American” as the file.

### Adjacent doors

Rohingya is not Burmese by default. Mon, Kachin, Karenni — ask. Some households are mixed.

Ask this household. Never one Asian module. Never one Burma interpreter.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Burmese cultural community (umbrella): 17,123; Twin Cities 79.9%; Greater Minnesota 20.1%; age 17 or younger 41.5%; 65+ 4.2%; foreign-born 67.1%; language other than English (age 5+) 89.6%; English less than “very well” 67.0%; high school or higher (25+) 32.8%; bachelor’s or higher 11.8%; less than high school (25+) 67.2%; median household income about $75,513 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 29.6%; owner-occupied 59.0%; renter-occupied 41.0%; average household size 4.99; disability 12.9%; uninsured 6.2%; households 3,655.

### Counts

Census recodes some Karen write-ins as Burmese. This is an administrative umbrella, not a people-count. Date Compass.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality. 67 percent LEP is a gate. 67 percent less than high school among 25+ is camp years, not a character. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass Burmese profile (ACS 2019–2023). Compass cultural-communities methodology (Karen recoded as Burmese). CLAS fifteen interpreter cards: Burmese. Karen Organization of Minnesota — a Karen door, not automatically this page. Churches, monasteries, and mosques families name. Burmese, Chin, and Rohingya groups they name. Pay that partner. MSP Magazine on Minnesota’s refugee history (1993 Burma-origin arrivals; Greater MN towns).

### Public doors

CECLC is a door, not the whole community. Learn on your own time. Do not make a Burmese, Chin, or Karen colleague your unpaid tutor.

### Learn on your own time

Report back. Guest. Name the town.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Who is in the room: Bamar, Chin, Karen, Rohingya, Mon, Kachin. An interpreter labeled Burmese for a Hakha Chin household is a closed door. If Karen, open Karen Minnesota. If Rohingya, Burmese is not the default language. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

67 percent LEP: the severe language gate. Literacy of the form is a second gate — Burmese script is not guaranteed. English IEP for a parent who does not read it is a closed door.

Greater Minnesota: 20.1 percent. Worthington and other plant towns. An eList and an English PDF from St. Paul is not how this household was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: camp years and interrupted schooling are structure. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a risk score.

Workforce: Burmese, Chin, and Karen staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community.

Asian mash is a closed gate. Not Hmong. Not Karen as a synonym.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that heard “Burmese” and booked the country.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about Cambodian / Khmer people as a people with a long state history on the Mekong and a Minnesota community built after the Khmer Rouge. Pronounce Khmer. A common English rendering is kuh-MARE. Then ask. If you say “Cambodian” as if it were interchangeable with Hmong or Vietnamese, you have already told the household you did not study.

### Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. It is not Lao. It is not Thai. It is not a generic Southeast Asian interpreter. Shared continent is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Cambodian cultural community near 11,984. About 73.8 percent Twin Cities, 26.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 27.7 percent age 17 or younger; 11.0 percent 65+. About 50.5 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 61.2 percent; English less than “very well” 29.4 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A survivor of 1975–1979 who came through a Thai camp, a Christian grandmother, a monk whose wat is the civic center, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota household the building forgot, a college student who uses English with friends and Khmer with an elder — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Khmer peoplehood is older than the refugee file and older than the French protectorate. The Khmer Empire — Angkor as literacy for the desk, not a tourism sentence — is a state history with writing, irrigation, and monumental architecture. Khmer language and Khmer script are not oral-only. That matters when an English form meets an elder who reads Khmer, and when it meets an elder who does not.

### History for the meeting

French colonial rule, independence (1953), Sihanouk, Lon Nol, and then 1975 are the modern political sequence. 1975–1979 is the foundational political event of Cambodian Minnesota. It is not the origin of the people.

### What people brought

What people brought: language and script, Theravada Buddhism and ancestor practice, farming knowledge, kinship, and a memory of a state that ate its own. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled anything but Khmer.

Do not start with embroidery or Angkor Wat as icebreaker. History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Khmer World
sections.body:
Homeland is Cambodia — the Mekong, Tonle Sap, Phnom Penh, the provinces people name. Khmer people also live in the Mekong delta and in a global diaspora: California (Long Beach among the named U.S. hubs), Massachusetts, Minnesota, France, Australia. Thai border camps — Khao-I-Dang and others — are exile geography, not home.

### Homeland

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): 73.8 percent Twin Cities, 26.2 percent Greater Minnesota. Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought. Watt Munisotaram stands in Empire Township / Hampton, Dakota County — Twin Cities metro, a wat on farmland, not a downtown festival.

### Minnesota

Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Cambodia. Secondary migration built parts of this map.

sections.heading: Khmer Rouge, 1975–1979, and the Camps — Foundational Event
sections.body:
If the Secret War is the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, the Khmer Rouge years 1975–1979 and the Killing Fields are the foundational event of Cambodian Minnesota.

### Foundational events

17 April 1975: Phnom Penh fell. The Khmer Rouge emptied cities, abolished money and schools, murdered intellectuals, monks, and anyone marked as enemy, and worked and starved the rest. 1975–1979 is not a personality. It is not an icebreaker. Do not ask a survivor to narrate killing for your professional development.

### Who you meet

Vietnamese invasion, 1979. Camps in Thailand. Resettlement to the United States in the late 1970s and 1980s through voluntary agencies and churches. Secondary migration. The desk in 2026 also meets their children — U.S.-born, English-dominant with peers, still translating for parents, still unable to get Khmer in the lobby.

U.S. policy later deported people with certain convictions, including people who have lived here since childhood. That is current structure. Do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Households are often larger than a nuclear English form. Compass: average household size 3.28 (ACS 2019–2023). Elders, adult children, and obligation sit in the same week. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox.

### Who is in the household

Ask who should be in the room. A nuclear English form already has a who.

### Who speaks

Khmer names on U.S. forms get split wrong. Family name often comes first in Khmer order and last in the file. Ask order. Do not treat unmatched last names as fraud by default.

Women’s labor — factory, business, professional second generation — sits next to elder authority. Both can be true in the same room.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Cambodian History
sections.body:
This department will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota (26.2 percent is not an afterthought).

### Places

Partners: United Cambodian Association of Minnesota historically; Watt Munisotaram in Empire / Hampton, Dakota County — among the largest Cambodian Buddhist temples in the United States, established 1982; other wats families name. CECLC is a door, not the whole community.

### Partners

Public calendar: Khmer New Year in April; Pchum Ben; 17 April as genocide remembrance. A calendar click is not community engagement. Guest at the wat. Shoes. Head. Altar.

Cambodian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A New Year visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Khmer — the heart of a people
sections.body:
To be Khmer in Minnesota is to be a people with a state history and a catastrophe, filed under a U.S. racial checkbox that also holds Hmong, Chinese, Indian, and Korean histories they do not share. Face, elder obligation, and the wat travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

1975–1979 sits in some rooms as living memory and in some rooms as a school unit the grandchild studied. Do not assume which. Do not make it a personality.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Khmer language and Khmer script. Not Hmong. Not Vietnamese. Not Lao. Literacy in Khmer is not guaranteed for every elder. The English form is still a gate.

### Wat

Theravada Buddhist temple as civic and ritual center for many. Do not make a monk the case plan unless this family asked.

Ancestors and spirit practice sit beside Buddhism and, in some families, Christianity. An altar in a living room is not a case plan and not a museum.

### Face and harmony

Direct refusal may be costly. A yes that is courtesy is not a signature.

1975–1979. Living memory in a waiver meeting is not an icebreaker. You do not use it. You know it so you do not trample it.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
sections.body:
Theravada Buddhism is central for many Cambodian Minnesota families. The wat is civic and ritual. Christianity lives in some families — sometimes in the same cousin-line as a Buddhist altar. Spirit and ancestor practice are not “extra.”

### Streams

Do not make a monk the case plan unless this family asked. Do not treat Buddhism as decoration, and do not treat church as the evolved version.

### Practice

Shoes off at the wat and in many homes. The head is high; do not touch it. Feet are low; do not point them at an altar, a Buddha, or a person. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence. Trauma and under-identified mental health sit in this community’s U.S. literature. Date what you cite. Do not invent a rate.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
