That founding is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not permission to fold this household into historic African American cultural intelligence because some founders came from the United States.

### History for the meeting

Indigenous Liberian nations were not a blank coast. Mission schools, English as official language, and a coastal/settler and hinterland split still sit in some rooms. Ask which people they are. Do not lecture Americo-Liberian taxonomy they did not ask for.

### What people brought

What people brought: English and Liberian English, ethnic languages, church and mosque, rice as ordinary food, kin obligation, a memory of a state that broke. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Black” checkbox, and often the historic African American page because the building heard English.

Origins did not begin in the civil war. The war is the foundational event of much of the Minnesota community you will meet. It is not a personality.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Liberian World
sections.body:
Liberia is counties and peoples, not a blob. Monrovia is not the whole. A person may name a county, a town, a people — Kpelle in Bong, Bassa on the coast, Gio in Nimba — not the capital. Confirm if it matters. Do not referee county politics in a waiver meeting.

### Homeland

The diaspora is U.S.-heavy: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, New York, Georgia, and others. Minnesota is a real hub, not the only one. Secondary migration built part of what you will meet here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass 90.5 percent Twin Cities, 9.5 percent Greater Minnesota. Brooklyn Park and Brooklyn Center are local knowledge of concentration — confirm on this family. Do not assume that city is the whole. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Liberia. Inner-ring suburbs and Greater Minnesota towns with work and housing are still this people.

sections.heading: Civil Wars, TPS, DED, and LRIF — Foundational Event
sections.body:
If 1975 is Vietnamese Minnesota’s foundational event, the Liberian civil wars are the foundational event of much of Liberian Minnesota.

### Foundational events

Samuel Doe, the 1980 coup, Charles Taylor, roughly 1989–1997 and 1999–2003. Dead in the hundreds of thousands. Displacement. Camps in Guinea, Côte d’Ivoire, Sierra Leone, Ghana. Child soldiers in some rooms as history, not a file you open as a risk score. Most people were not fighters. Most people were trying to live.

### Who you meet

The United States granted Temporary Protected Status, then Deferred Enforced Departure, and left people in temporary status for decades. Liberian Refugee Immigration Fairness (2019) opened a path some families used. That climate still sits in who opens the door. Family reunification and ordinary immigration are later streams. The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children — English-dominant with peers, still translating for a grandmother whose English is Kolokwa, still filed under Black.

The war is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Extended households and elder authority sit in many rooms. Country kin, town kin, church kin. Compass average household size about 3.49. Not always a nuclear English form. Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a sister, a cousin, a church mother, not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who is in the household

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with Minnesota English. That child is not the qualified interpreter even when Compass says English only 80.3 percent. CLAS still stands if this elder needs Liberian English. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book the interpreter. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who speaks

Women’s labor — care, nursing, CNA, shop, professional second generation — sits next to elder obligation. Both can be true in the same room. Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Liberian History
sections.body:
Minnesota holds a Liberian community large enough for a Compass row and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Compass: about 20,720 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 9.5 percent. Do not write this people as a Brooklyn Park anecdote until this family lives there.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Brooklyn Park and Brooklyn Center as named concentration in local knowledge — confirm on this family; inner-ring suburbs; Minneapolis and St. Paul pockets; Greater Minnesota towns with work and housing. Churches are public life. They are not consultation. A food visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: Liberian Community of Minnesota / Liberian Community Center historically; churches families name; CECLC as a department door — not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Liberian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Independence Day (26 July) is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Liberian Minnesota — the heart of a people
sections.body:
To be Liberian in Minnesota is to be a West African people with English as an official language, filed under Black by a building that already has a historic African American page and thinks the work is done. Face, elder obligation, church, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

The civil war sits in the room for some and is a history class for others. First-wave survivors, later arrivals, U.S.-born children, Mandingo and Kpelle and Americo-Liberian families do not share one Tuesday. You do not referee. You do not put “child soldier” on a case note as color.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: many Liberian Minnesotans are Black in a racial order that also holds historic African American, Somali, Nigerian, and Kenyan histories they do not share. The mash is the gate.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Which people inside Liberia. Kpelle, Bassa, Gio, Kru, Grebo, Vai, Mandingo, Krahn, Americo-Liberian, others. Ask. The Compass row is not the ethnic file.

### English and Liberian English

Official English is not Minnesota professional English. Kolokwa in some rooms. Ethnic languages in some homes. “English” on the interpreter line can still be a closed door.

### Civil war memory

Foundational for the community. Not a personality for the person in the lobby.

### Church as channel

Pentecostal, Protestant, Catholic. Islam in some families. Do not make clergy the case plan unless they asked.

### DED / TPS / LRIF climate

Temporary status for decades is structure. Do not collect status you do not need.

### Not historic African American

Shared race and shared English are not shared culture.

sections.heading: Religion
sections.body:
Christianity is the large public stream in Liberian Minnesota: Protestant, Pentecostal, Catholic. Islam lives in Mandingo and other families. Traditional practice sits in some rooms and is not a souvenir. None is also a Tuesday. Ask.

### Streams

The church is a center of ritual, mutual aid, information, and sometimes the only institution that found this family after the war. It is not “the community.” Do not BCC one pastor and call it consultation. Do not make clergy the case plan unless this family asked. Do not copy historic African American church honorifics as if they were this grammar. Follow this room.

### Practice

Funerals gather family and can run long. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Do not treat traditional practice as horror-film content. Do not treat a Pentecostal fast as noncompliance with a med until you have asked.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Elders first. English “hello” is ordinary. Liberian English greetings live in some rooms — follow this room; do not perform one you learned from a video. Handshake in many professional rooms. Church titles (Reverend, Deacon, Mother) in some rooms — use them until invited not to.

### Titles

A hard handshake you assume is universal is already a closed door for some women and some elders. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. If a hand is not offered, nod. Do not force it.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules onto this page. Do not assume the Black nod is this grammar. It may appear in a U.S. racial room. It is not the file.

Physical contact: ask the room. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it. Say the name.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
English and biblical given names are common — James, Mary, Washington, Cooper — because of mission schools, the settler republic, and English as official language. Country names and ethnic names also live here. A person may use an English name at the desk and another name at home. Ask which name they use on this file.

### How to file

U.S. forms want first-middle-last. Liberian naming may not match. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not “correct” a Liberian English spelling to U.S. school English. The form that guesses will invent a person, and that invented name follows them through MHCP, school, and child welfare.

Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason. Do not joke about names that sound “American.” They are Liberian names too.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
Independence Day — 26 July — is the large annual public date. Travel, food, church, closed shops in some pockets. Schedule around it when you can. Guest if invited. A calendar click is not community engagement.

### Calendar

Church calendars — Easter, Christmas, harvest, watch night — are ordinary. Muslim dates in Mandingo and other rooms. Ask.

Civil-war anniversaries some families name and some refuse. Do not put a war date on a case note as color. Do not collect it as a risk score.

Do not put “African holiday” on a case note. Ordinary U.S. holidays are real in the second generation. Ask this family.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Liberian Minnesotans 25 and older, about 90.2 percent high school or higher; about 29.5 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 63.2 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Liberian English and limited Minnesota professional English is not illiterate. The form written for a historic African American household, or for a white Minnesota reader, can still be a closed door. Kolokwa in the home is not “broken English.” Put Liberian English on the interpreter line if this household needs it.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus a school that never learned the name. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter. The child is not the interpreter.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Elders first. Hospitality is a virtue in many rooms. Accept a little food if offered. Rice and soup are ordinary, not a festival. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Shoes off in some homes. Church time can run long. Do not photograph a family and call it rapport. Do not enter a prayer space as a tour.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the English they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter if this elder needs Liberian English.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
English is Liberia’s official language. Liberian English and Kolokwa (Liberian Kreyol) are not Minnesota professional English. An interpreter labeled English who does not hear this elder is a closed door. Ethnic languages — Kpelle, Bassa, and others — live in some homes. Ask. Book the language this household names.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 80.3 percent English only; about 19.7 percent a language other than English; about 8.7 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. English-only 80.3 percent is not proof the form was heard. Second-generation Minnesota English is common. The IEP still has to reach the parent.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Liberian coworker the interpreter. Do not write “broken English” on a file.

sections.heading: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Civil-war trauma is real in some rooms: killing, camps, rape as a weapon of war, child-soldier history. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to skip screening. It is a reason a government badge is not automatically help. Do not put “child soldier” on a case note as color. Do not mash this into a historic African American crime narrative.

DED, TPS, and the decades of temporary status are current structure for some, even after LRIF. It changes who opens the door. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

Compass poverty 20.9 percent is dated. It is not a race trait and not a personality. Care-work wages and renter 68.8 percent are labor and housing facts.

LGBTQ Liberian Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Liberia’s own law climate is not Minnesota’s. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent African stoicism. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee. This is not the historic African American page. Shared race is not shared medical history.

### Access

Hepatitis B screening for people born in Liberia is a U.S. public-health pattern — CDC has treated Liberia as a higher-prevalence birth country in screening guidance. Date the CDC page you cite. Do not invent a Minnesota rate. Do not skip screening because the person looks well.

Compass disability 3.9 percent — dated. Poverty 20.9 percent is context for delayed care, not a personality. War trauma, depression, and somatic presentation exist. Mental-health stigma is real in some families. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9.

Traditional medicine and church healing often sit beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. FGC exists in some Liberian ethnic communities. Minnesota law stands. Do not invent a rate. Do not mash the Somali page here. Do not skip care. Late help-seeking can be language, stigma, status climate, and a lobby that already used a child as the interpreter.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Liberian Minnesotans exist. Conservative family and church climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Liberian life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. Liberia’s law climate is not this state’s. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

War memory and church do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Country cloth, lappa, and formal dress are public at Independence Day, weddings, and some church stages. They are not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

This is not the CROWN Act chapter as the file — and anti-Blackness still sits on Liberian bodies in U.S. clinics, schools, and traffic stops. Ask this person. Do not mash historic African American hair politics as a script, and do not ignore them.

Do not touch. Gold, a church hat, a wedding cloth — not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table. Care-work and nursing may mean a uniform. That is labor. It is not a personality.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Gospel, church choir, highlife, hipco, diaspora pop, reggae as regional listening in some rooms. Independence stages hold more than one of these. Named variation, not a playlist.

### Variation

A funeral is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement. Knowing that war memory can sit inside a song will stop you from putting the wrong joke on a speaker.

Independence stages are public life. They are not consultation and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Soccer is public Liberian life. George Weah is a public image of the country. He is not a personality you assign a child in clinic. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Basketball shows up.

### Not the whole person

Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see. Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some. They are not language access and not a case plan.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday if this elder needs Liberian English.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
English made a written public. Oral forms, church writing, and Liberian English as the literature of the everyday sit beside it. Minnesota and U.S. Liberian writers and journalists exist. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do need to know this is not a people without letters. Many elders read English. Some do not. A notice written only in Minnesota professional English can still be a closed door for a Kolokwa speaker. Ask.

Do not write “illiterate” because the English is not yours. Write what they tell you.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Country cloth, carving, church pageantry, Independence public culture. Rice, soup, and pepper are foodway, not consultation.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. A church or community-center visit is optional professional development. It is not consultation. Do not photograph a family as tourism.

Heritage Month that mashes this with historic African American quilts, a Somali poster, or one “African” table has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

sections.heading: War, Temporary Status, and the State
sections.body:
The 1980 coup, two civil wars roughly 1989–2003, camps, TPS then DED, and a United States that left people in temporary status for decades until LRIF in 2019 — that is the political event. Later: policing, and enforcement climate for people still without a stable status. A DHS badge is not automatically help.

### The badge

Do not use the war as a personality. Do not ask a survivor to narrate killing for your professional development. Do not put child-soldier history on a case note as color. Intra-community politics about the war and about who came when are real. You do not referee them on a file.

DED/TPS climate changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not mash this chapter into historic African American CRM because both are Black.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Care work, CNA, nursing, shop, restaurant, factory, professional second generation, public employment. Compass median household income about $59,903; poverty 20.9 percent; renter 68.8 percent — dated. Nursing and CNA labor is a documented Liberian American work pattern in some rooms. It is work. It is not a personality, not a joke, and not the whole economy.

### Work

Liberian staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Staff

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision. Pay the partner this household names.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
English versus Liberian English is the first failure the building will miss because the checkbox says English. Confirm this English. Book Liberian English if this elder needs it. Still book a qualified interpreter when language is the gate. Do not use a child. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### Language

Who is in the room. A child pushed forward as Minnesota English. A pastor in the story. Pain you must believe. War trauma you do not make a personality. DED/TPS climate. A nuclear form that filed them under Black and opened the historic African American page.

### The meeting

Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Ask which name they use. If they name church healing or traditional medicine, listen. Mandated reporting still exists. Believe reported pain. Do not invent African stoicism. Do not mix Tuskegee into this history as the file.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not historic African American / Black American. Compass African American includes some Liberian ancestry that other counts exclude. That mash is not this page. Open historic African American for a Great Migration household. Open this for Liberian.

### Adjacent doors

Not Somali. Not Nigerian as a synonym — related West African coast, different state, different war, different languages. Not Sierra Leonean as mash: related war, different republic. Not Ghanaian. Never one Black module. Never one “African” interpreter.

Some households are mixed. Some Liberian families have historic African American in-laws. Ask this household. Shared race is not shared culture. Shared English is not shared English.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Liberian cultural community: about 20,720; Twin Cities 90.5%; Greater Minnesota 9.5%; age 17 or younger 43.7%; 65+ 4.4%; foreign-born 63.2%; English only (age 5+) 80.3%; language other than English 19.7%; English less than “very well” 8.7%; high school or higher (25+) 90.2%; bachelor’s or higher 29.5%; median household income about $59,903 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 20.9%; owner-occupied 31.2%; renter-occupied 68.8%; average household size 3.49; disability 3.9%.

### Counts

Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions (ancestry vs. birthplace vs. the Compass African American mash that includes some Liberian ancestry). Date the number you cite. This page is Liberian Minnesota, not that mash.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality. English-only 80.3 percent is not proof the elder heard the form. Poverty is not a race trait. Language and child-as-interpreter are still gates. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass Liberian profile (ACS 2019–2023). Compass African American profile — some Liberian ancestry in that mash; this page is not that mash. Liberian Community of Minnesota / Liberian Community Center historically. Churches families name. Brooklyn Park / Brooklyn Center as local knowledge of concentration — confirm on this family.

### Public doors

CECLC is a door, not the whole community. An eList is not engagement. Pay partners. Report back.

### Learn on your own time

Learn on your own time. Do not make a Liberian colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC a church and call it consultation. Guest at Independence Day if invited — it is not consultation.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled English who does not speak Liberian English as this elder speaks it is a closed door. Compass English-only 80.3 percent is not proof the packet was heard. Still book a qualified interpreter when language is the gate. Do not use a child. Do not write “broken English.” Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: English names that look “American” are still Liberian names. The database that “corrects” spelling invents a person.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without the English this household uses are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. War trauma is not a risk score. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a historic African American crime narrative. Do not invent African stoicism.

DED/TPS/LRIF climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF written for a white or historic African American reader is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 9.5 percent. Brooklyn Park is not the whole channel until this family lives there.

Workforce: Liberian staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Black mash: opening historic African American because both are Black and both speak English is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that filed Liberian under Black and never learned Kolokwa.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about Mexican Minnesota — mexicano, mexicana. It is the largest Latino origin in this state. Mexico is many peoples. Mixtec (Ñuu Savi) and Zapotec (Benizaa) may be in the home here. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door.

### Who this is

Mexican Minnesota. Not the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. Not a synonym for every Spanish-surnamed household in the lobby. Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Mexican cultural community at 229,576. Twin Cities 61.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent — nearly 4 in 10 live outside the Twin Cities (Compass Points 2023). About 38.0 percent age 17 or younger; 4.0 percent 65+. Foreign-born 26.7 percent — a majority in that vintage were born here. Language other than English (age 5+) 58.3 percent; English less than “very well” 23.7 percent. Date the number you use. Mixtec and Zapotec may be in the home; Compass does not count speakers. Do not invent that count. A rate is not the person.

### Who this is not

This is not Guatemalan. It is not Salvadoran. It is not Puerto Rican. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent. That page is the mash and the CLAS Spanish line. This page is Mexican. If you file the household under “Latino” because the checkbox was easier, you have left this door.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. A Mixtec dairy worker in a southern county, a U.S.-born professional in a first-ring suburb, a West Side elder whose family has been in St. Paul longer than your unit, a Jalisco restaurant household, a college student who uses English with friends and Spanish with a grandmother, a person who will not open the door because a relative can be moved — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

Always defer to the person in front of you. The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well — how family is named, what respect looks like, what a greeting carries, what a form may land on. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Mexican peoplehood is older than the Bracero program, older than IRCA, and older than the Minnesota plant.

### Many peoples

A country on the land between the United States and Guatemala. Mestizo majority narratives. Mixtec, Zapotec, Purépecha, Maya in the south, and other indigenous nations whose languages may be in a Minnesota home. Ask. Do not lecture a Worthington family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, independence (the Grito of 16 September 1810; consummation 1821), the Revolution after 1910, and a modern republic that has both claimed and erased indigenous nations — that is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with food, a sombrero, or a Heritage Month sentence.

Writing in Spanish is the ordinary public literacy of the Mexican state. Mixtec and Zapotec are languages, not dialects of Spanish. Some elders read Spanish. Some do not. Some U.S.-born adults do not read Spanish either. Oral skill is not print.

### What people brought

Language (Spanish varieties and indigenous languages), kinship, parish and later evangelical church, farm and trade skill, Guadalupe, a memory of a border that used them. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” checkbox, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a rural plant town or a St. Paul lobby that had not studied Mixtec.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Mexican World
sections.body:
Mexico is not one climate and not one Spanish.

### Mexico

North, center, south; Oaxaca, Michoacán, Jalisco, Guanajuato, the border states, Mexico City — tones, food, and some vocabulary shift. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Monterrey versus Oaxaca in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a pueblo.

### United States and Minnesota

The U.S. Mexican map is California, Texas, Illinois, the Southwest, and also the Upper Midwest plant and dairy counties that a Minneapolis default still treats as leftover. Compass: 61.1 percent Twin Cities, 38.9 percent Greater Minnesota. Nearly 4 in 10 (Compass Points 2023). Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, and dairy counties are names you should be able to hold without turning them into a tour.

### Metro

West Side St. Paul / District del Sol is historic Mexican Minnesota, not a museum. Lake Street and Phillips, first-ring suburbs, scattered apartments near plants. Do not assume West Side. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Mexico. A Greater Minnesota household is still this people.

sections.heading: Labor, IRCA, and Enforcement — Foundational Events
sections.body:
If 1975 is the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota, Mexican Minnesota is stacked.

### Labor and settlement

Labor recruitment into sugar beet, cannery, and later plants and dairy. The Bracero program (1942–1964) as U.S. policy literacy. IRCA-era settlement after 1986. Later family and work streams. Enforcement waves that reorganize who will open the door. This is not a Guatemalan war file and not a Salvadoran TPS file.

Mexican migrant farm labor in Minnesota is older than the current plant map. Settlement followed work, church, and IRCA. Secondary migration pulled kin.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 does not only meet a first wave. It meets U.S.-born children — Compass foreign-born 26.7 percent — translating for parents, mixed-status households, and a Mixtec household that has been in a dairy county for years and still cannot get Mixtec in the lobby.

### Enforcement

Enforcement is current structure. When raids, rumored raids, or a visible ICE climate spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. A notice mailed to a household afraid to open the door is a closed gate. Do not collect status you do not need. The desk that asks “are you legal?” on visit one has already chosen a who.

If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss the majority born here and still treat the English IEP as culturally neutral.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Familismo is a hypothesis, not a personality. Elders often speak first.

### Who is in the household

Adult children may be in the same week as a waiver meeting, a plant shift, and a school conference. Compass: average household size about 3.09. Still not always a nuclear English form. Grandparents may be the household. Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a son, a daughter-in-law, a sibling, a padrino — not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox.

Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Mixed-status

Mixed-status is structure: a U.S.-citizen child, a parent without status, a sibling with DACA, an aunt who works the plant. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. CLAS still stands. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm: it reverses respeto, it leaks adult business, and it is not language access. Book the interpreter. Ask who should be in the room.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Mexican History
sections.body:
Minnesota holds the largest Latino-origin community in the state. Compass: 229,576 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 38.9 percent — nearly 4 in 10 (Compass Points 2023). Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote. Human services will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment, in a plant town and on the West Side.

### Places

West Side St. Paul / District del Sol — historic Mexican Minnesota, not a museum. Lake Street and Phillips. First-ring suburbs. Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, dairy counties, southern and western towns. Markets and taquerías are public life. They are not consultation. A food-court visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

CLUES — Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio (https://clues.org/). Centro Tyrone Guzmán. Rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. Churches are often the actual safe channel. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Mexican staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A fiesta or a Guadalupe mass is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Mexicano — the heart of a people
sections.body:
To be Mexican in Minnesota is to be a people with a country, indigenous nations inside that country, and a long memory of labor that built someone else’s harvest, then building a life in a cold state that filed you under Latino.

### Face and kin

Face, kin obligation, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

Mixtec and Zapotec peoplehood is not a dialect note. A household that names Mixtec is not “Mexican Spanish with an accent.” The mash is the gate.

### Under a Latino checkbox

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: Mexican Minnesota is the largest origin under a Latino checkbox that also holds Guatemalan, Salvadoran, Puerto Rican, and Andean histories they do not share. The Mexican default in this state is a count fact. It becomes a harm when the building treats this page as the only Latino file.

This brief is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
These concepts recur. They are hypotheses you still test on this family.

### Familismo

Kin as the unit of decision and care. Hypothesis, not a rule. The person who talks in the lobby may not be the person who decides. Ask who should be in the room. Not a license to skip mandated reporting. Staff do not use it as a guilt tool.

### Respeto

Titles, elders, usted. A first-name lobby and a joking tone can read as contempt. Follow this room. A courtesy-yes is not a signature. Ask again, plainly, without humiliation.

### Personalismo and confianza

Relationship before a long form. The first visit may be about whether you are safe. That is not delay. The clock still exists for medical and legal time. Enforcement climate, a bad interpreter, a child used as the mouth, an SSN field that feels like a trap — these spend confianza before you have it.

### Two surnames

Apellido paterno then apellido materno. The database that keeps one invents a person.

### Mixtec and Zapotec

Peoples and languages. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Compass does not count speakers. Ask.

Work, school, Guadalupe, mixed-status. A plant shift and a second-generation degree can sit in the same household. Do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Religion
sections.body:
Catholic majority in many Mexican Minnesota streams — not all.

### Parish and church

Our Lady of Guadalupe (12 December) is central in many Catholic lives. The parish may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, baptismal records, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Evangelical and Pentecostal churches are large. Indigenous practice lives in some Mixtec and Zapotec homes and is not a souvenir.

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a curandero the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or indigenous practice as witchcraft.

### Calendar and public history

Día de los Muertos is public history — ofrendas, 1–2 November — not a file and not a personality. Holy Week, quinceañera as religious-family event, Las Posadas, and funeral obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an ofrenda or a Guadalupe altar.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an older person is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth.

### Titles

Some streams greet familiars with a cheek kiss — follow this room; do not initiate because a training slide said Latinos are tactile.

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted versus tú is respect in Spanish; a qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Mexican Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno.

### Two surnames

José Luis García Hernández is not “José García” with leftover words. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Do not anglicize Jesús, Muñoz, Ñ as a convenience. Given names may be Spanish, Mixtec, Zapotec, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

### How to file

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records; some add de plus the husband’s paternal surname; some keep both family surnames. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
A calendar click is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement.

### Independence and Guadalupe

16 September — Mexican independence. Literacy for the meeting. Cinco de Mayo is the Battle of Puebla (1862), not independence, and not a party you put on a case note as the national day. Do not file this household under a restaurant calendar.

12 December — Our Lady of Guadalupe. Major for many Mexican Catholic families. Las Posadas in some streams (mid-December). Día de los Reyes / Three Kings — 6 January. Holy Week. Quinceañera is family-religious time, not a case note.

### Día de los Muertos

1–2 November. Public history in Minnesota. Guest if you are in a public ofrenda space. Not a file. Not a costume for staff.

Hispanic Heritage Month (15 September–15 October) is the umbrella calendar. It is not this people’s day and not consultation. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Mexican Minnesotans 25 and older, about 71.5 percent high school or higher; about 18.9 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 26.7 percent of the community is foreign-born.

### School and language

A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

A parent who speaks fluent Spanish, or fluent Mixtec, and limited English is not illiterate. Some elders read Spanish. Some do not. Mixtec or Zapotec in the home is not a Spanish IEP. The English-only form is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.

### Mobility and gap

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Elders first. Titles. Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an ofrenda or a Guadalupe altar. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain “your culture” as entertainment. Shoes: follow the household.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic, plant shifts, and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Mexican Spanish is not Salvadoran Spanish, not Caribbean Spanish, and not one interpreter accent test.

### Spanish

Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. Register matters: usted, not a buddy tú, until the room says otherwise.

### Mixtec and Zapotec

Mixtec and Zapotec may be in the home. Compass notes the language possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count. A Spanish interpreter for those households is still a closed door. Name the language on the request. A scarce interpreter is a gate, not an excuse to proceed in English only without recording the gap.

### What Compass shows

Among those 5 and older, about 58.3 percent speak a language other than English; about 23.7 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Many U.S.-born people use English with peers and Spanish with an elder. The IEP still has to reach the parent. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed: oral skill is not print.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Mexican coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Enforcement

ICE and enforcement climate is structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate.

### Named harms

Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is a named harm. Mixtec, Zapotec. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Colorism is real. Intra-Latino hierarchy is real: the Mexican default in this state will talk over a Maya or Caribbean household if you let the umbrella page do this page’s job — and this page will talk over Mixtec if you let mestizo Spanish be the only file.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Who speaks in the meeting, who holds the papers, who is allowed to leave the house — ask, and follow law. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Mexican Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it familismo. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent “Latino stoicism” or “they are dramatic.” Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic immigrant-mistrust slide.

### Patterns to date

U.S. public-health literature has treated Mexican-origin adults as a higher-prevalence group for type 2 diabetes — date the CDC page you cite. Do not invent a Minnesota rate. Do not skip screening because the person looks well. Uninsured and delayed-care patterns sit here. Date Minnesota figures when you have them. Compass poverty (ACS 2019–2023) is 12.8 percent — a poverty figure, not an uninsured rate.

### Access

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish or this Mixtec — these are clinical events. When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Traditional medicine, yerberías, and parish prayer can sit next to a fierce wish for biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Do not mock. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter in a health encounter. Mental-health stigma is real in some families. A smile is not a PHQ-9.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Mexican Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, parish, and evangelical climates can mean silence or exile. Mixtec and Zapotec queer people exist.

### This person

Some people live a public English life and a private Spanish or Mixtec life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit. Familismo is not a license to call kin. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

Face and parish climate do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
There is no Mexican uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota.

### Dress

Mixtec and Zapotec dress is public at fiesta and ceremony, not a daily costume, and not yours to request for a Heritage Month photo. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

Colorism and hair texture are real. Mestizo default beauty is a hierarchy. Name it if it is in the room. Do not rank. Do not touch.

Quinceañera dress, baptism white, funeral black, evangelical modesty, a Guadalupe medal — celebration and devotion, not a case note. Plant and dairy work may mean stained hands. That is labor. It is not a joke and not a race trait.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Mariachi, ranchera, norteño, banda, cumbia, corridos, church music. Named variation, not a playlist.

### Variation

A Mexican default playlist in a Guatemalan or Puerto Rican waiting room is the mash in speakers. This page is Mexican; still do not assume norteño is this household.

Corridos include narcocorridos in some streams. That is a named fact, not a joke and not a risk score you write on a last name.

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. A funeral is not staff entertainment. Guadalupe mañanitas are public life. They are not consultation and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Fútbol is the default public sport for many boys and men, and for many girls. Boxing has prestige in some streams. School sport is ordinary for the second generation.

### Not the whole person

Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

Leagues and pickup games are social infrastructure in metro and in plant towns. They are not language access and not a case plan. Greater Minnesota teams are still this people.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
Spanish-language literature is world literature. Mixtec and Zapotec oral literature is older than the Spanish file and is not “no letters.”

### Literacy in the lobby

That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.

Minnesota has Mexican and Chicano journalists, poets, and scholars. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know this is not a people without letters, and not a people who can all read the exception process.

Print Spanish from Spain or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish. CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Murals on the West Side and on Lake Street are public Minnesota art, not a booth. Ofrendas at Día de los Muertos are public history. Mixtec and Zapotec weaving are art and memory, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. Do not photograph an altar because it is pretty. An ofrenda is not a case plan. A mural tour is not consultation. Markets and taquerías are foodway, not consultation.

Heritage Month that mashes this with a generic Latino playlist or a Guatemalan traje has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

sections.heading: Labor, Enforcement, and the State
sections.body:
The political literacy here is labor and the border, not a single civil war.

### Labor and the badge

U.S. recruitment, Bracero, IRCA 1986 and settlement, and enforcement that reorganizes Tuesday. A DHS badge is not automatically help. That is not paranoia. It is pattern.

When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. Do not tell people the climate is fine so the form is fair now. Do not use a crossing or a raid as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate the desert for your professional development.

### Status

Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Notices to a household that will not open the door are a closed gate with a polite label. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a deportation score.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
sections.body:
Food processing, dairy, agriculture, construction, service, restaurants, cleaning, childcare, home care, professional second generation, public employment.

### Work

Rural plants and metro kitchens can sit in the same extended family. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same household.

Worker centers and parishes may be the trusted channel in Greater Minnesota. Name the local one. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume CLUES reaches a dairy county. Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice.

### Staff

Mexican staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters, not the Mixtec pool, and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan. Do not make a Mexican colleague your unpaid tutor.

Remittance to kin in Mexico is obligation for many, not a disposable luxury. A budget that treats it as optional has already chosen a household type.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
sections.body:
Language including indigenous. Book qualified Spanish AND ask.

### Language

Confirm Mixtec or Zapotec when that is the home language. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

Who is in the room. Gender match in maternal and intimate care if they want it. Titles. Two surnames. SSN on the first screen: if you do not need it, do not demand it as theater. Mixed-status: do not collect status you do not need. Enforcement climate: skipped appointments are pattern.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. If they name a healer or a parish, listen. Do not make either the case plan unless they asked. Mandated reporting still exists. Rural access is a gate: distance, clinic hours, one interpreter contracted from the Cities who does not speak this language. Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent is not an afterthought.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
sections.body:
Not the Latino / Hispanic umbrella.

### Adjacent doors

Open that brief as adjacent — CLAS Spanish, the mash, the other origins as a list. This page is Mexican. Do not file this household under “Latino” and call it done.

Not Guatemalan. Not Salvadoran. Not Puerto Rican. Not Ecuadorian, Colombian, Cuban, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Dominican, Venezuelan. Name the origin. Open the people brief that matches this household.

### Indigenous languages

Not Mixtec or Zapotec as “Mexican Spanish.” Those are languages and peoples. A Spanish interpreter is not those languages. Not Brazilian Portuguese. Not Somali. Not historic African American — Afro-Mexican people exist; ask, do not mash. Never one Latino module.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Mexican cultural community.

### Compass

229,576; Twin Cities 61.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent (nearly 4 in 10 — Compass Points 2023); age 17 or younger 38.0 percent; 65+ 4.0 percent; foreign-born 26.7 percent; language other than English (age 5+) 58.3 percent; English less than “very well” 23.7 percent; high school or higher (25+) 71.5 percent; bachelor’s or higher 18.9 percent; median household income about $66,000; poverty 12.8 percent; owner-occupied 53.2 percent; average household size 3.09; disability 8.4 percent.

### What Compass does not count

Mixtec, Zapotec may be in the home — Compass notes the language possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions (Hispanic origin vs. ancestry vs. language vs. birthplace). Date the number you cite.

A young age structure is not a personality. An owner rate is not proof the gates closed. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates. Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent is not an afterthought. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
sections.body:
Minnesota Compass Mexican profile (ACS 2019–2023) — https://www.mncompass.org/topics/demographics/cultural-communities/mexican. Date the retrieval.

### Public doors

Compass Points 2023 on the Greater Minnesota share. CLUES — Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio — https://clues.org/. Twin Cities services. Not the whole state. Centro Tyrone Guzmán — family and youth; metro. Rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. The parish in a dairy county may be the actual door.

CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Open the Latino umbrella brief as adjacent, not as this page. Open Guatemalan, Salvadoran, Puerto Rican when that is the household. Open a Mixtec or Zapotec interpreter request when Spanish is the wrong door.

### Learn on your own time

Do not make a Mexican colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC CLUES and call it consultation. Pay partners. Report back. Hispanic Heritage Month is not the work.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
sections.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. Mixtec and Zapotec may be in the home. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the language. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: two surnames. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

Hour caps, exception processes, SSN on the first screen, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral. Mixed-status households will bounce if the first field feels like enforcement. Do not collect status you do not need.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Enforcement climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 38.9 percent — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Mexican staff are not the interpreter pool, not the Mixtec pool, and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Latino mash: opening the umbrella, or Guatemalan or Salvadoran or Puerto Rican, because the checkbox says Hispanic is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned the second surname.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
sections.body:
This brief is about Nigerian Minnesota as a state-name community of many peoples. Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Edo, Ijaw, Tiv, Ibibio, Fulani, and others are not one file. Book the language this household names. English is official. Nigerian Pidgin is a language, not broken English. Yoruba is not Igbo. Hausa is not Yoruba. A “Nigerian interpreter” is not a language. An “African interpreter” is a closed door.

### Who this is

This is not Somali. Shared race in the United States is not shared culture. This is not historic African American. Compass African American is a different mash. This is not Liberian as a synonym — related West African coast, different state, different war, different languages. This is not Ghanaian.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Nigerian Minnesota near 18,141. About 87.6 percent Twin Cities, about 12.4 percent Greater Minnesota. About 29.9 percent age 17 or younger; about 8.2 percent 65+. About 60.3 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 55.7 percent; English less than “very well” 7.6 percent. Bachelor’s or higher (25+) 54.0 percent. Date the number. A rate is not the person. High attainment is not the interpreter.

The diversity inside this state name is the point. A Yoruba Pentecostal professional, an Igbo Catholic household that still names Biafra, a Hausa Muslim family, an Edo association member, a U.S.-born student who uses English with friends and Igbo with an elder, a Greater Minnesota nurse — share a Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
sections.body:
Nigeria is a state of many nations. Yoruba peoplehood in the southwest, Igbo peoplehood in the southeast, Hausa-Fulani in the north, Edo, Ijaw, Tiv, Ibibio, and hundreds of others. There is no single Nigerian ethnicity. Ask which people they are. Do not lecture taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

English as official language is colonial history. Independence in 1960. Biafra — 1967–1970 — is foundational literacy for many Igbo households. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not every Nigerian’s story. Do not referee it in a waiver meeting.

### What people brought

What people brought: ethnic language, English, Pidgin, church and mosque, titles, kin obligation, a memory of colony and of a civil war some will name and some will not. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “African” checkbox, one “Black” mash, and often Somali because the building already has that page.

Do not start with a Nollywood or jollof tourism sentence. Origins did not begin in Minneapolis.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Nigerian World
sections.body:
Homeland is not one map. Lagos and the Yoruba southwest, Igbo southeast, Hausa-Fulani north, Niger Delta, Middle Belt. Abuja is not the whole. A person may name Ibadan, Enugu, Kano, Benin City, Port Harcourt, a village — not the capital. Do not referee regional politics in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global and large: Texas, New York, Maryland and D.C., Georgia, the UK, the Gulf. Minnesota is a real community, not the U.S. capital of it. Secondary migration, church networks, school, and professional work pulled people here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass 87.6 percent Twin Cities, 12.4 percent Greater Minnesota. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume Cedar-Riverside. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Nigeria. Inner-ring suburbs and Greater Minnesota towns with hospitals and housing are still this people.

sections.heading: Independence, Biafra, and Later Streams — Foundational Events
sections.body:
There is no single 1975 or 1991 on this page. Independence in 1960 is the political founding of the state. Biafra, 1967–1970, is the foundational political event of much of Igbo Minnesota’s first memory. Dead in the millions by some counts. Famine as a weapon. That sentence is literacy. It is not a speech. It is not every Nigerian household.

### Foundational events

Later Minnesota streams are mixed: students, skilled work including healthcare, family reunification, diversity visas. Do not file every Nigerian household as refugee. Do not file every Nigerian household as a doctor. Both sit in this Compass row.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets first-generation professionals and U.S.-born children — English with peers, still translating for a grandmother whose Igbo or Yoruba was never booked, still filed under Black or under African.

If you only know “African,” you will miss this household.

sections.heading: Family
sections.body:
Family can be larger than a nuclear English form and can look like one. Compass average household size about 2.63 — smaller than Kenyan, Liberian, and Ethiopian Compass rows, dated, still not always Mary Jones. Elders often speak first. Titles — Chief, Obi, Igwe, Alhaji, Deacon — sit in some rooms. Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a sibling, an in-law, a church mother, not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox.

### Who is in the household

Hour caps and “natural supports” can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture. Naming is already a who: Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, English. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with Minnesota English. That child is not the qualified interpreter even when Compass LEP is 7.6 percent. CLAS still stands if this elder needs Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, or Pidgin. Ask who should be in the room. Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Nigerian History
sections.body:
Minnesota holds a Nigerian Compass community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment — and large enough that the building has a habit of hearing African and booking Somali or opening historic African American. Compass: about 18,141 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 12.4 percent. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities suburbs; Minneapolis and St. Paul pockets; Greater Minnesota towns with hospitals and housing. IgboFest as public life (including North Hennepin / Brooklyn Park in public listings). Churches are public life. They are not consultation. A jollof visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: Minnesota Institute for Nigerian Development (MIND) historically as an umbrella; Igbo associations and IgboFest; Yoruba, Edo, and other associations families name; churches and mosques families name; CECLC as a department door — not the whole. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Nigerian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. IgboFest or Independence Day is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Nigerian Minnesota — the heart of a people
sections.body:
To be Nigerian in Minnesota is to be a state-name people of many nations, filed under African, Black, and sometimes Somali by a building that has not studied. Peoplehood after colony, after Biafra for some, after oil and military rule, is not a Nollywood poster. Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, and the rest do not share one Tuesday. You do not pick a side.

### In this state

In this building another fact sits on top: many of these households are Black in a U.S. racial order that will file them under historic African American and get the language, the church, the title, and the name wrong. Shared race is not shared culture.

Face, elder obligation, titles, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.body:
Which people. Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Edo, others. Ask. The Compass row is not the ethnic file.

### Which language

Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Nigerian Pidgin, English, others. A “Nigerian interpreter” is not a language. An “African interpreter” is a closed door. Pidgin is a language, not broken English.

### Titles

Chief, Obi, Igwe, Alhaji, Deacon, Doctor. Use them until invited not to. They are not decoration.

### Faith is plural

Pentecostal, Catholic, Anglican, Islam, Ifá and Odinani in some rooms, none. Follow this room.

Do not referee Biafra or north/south politics in a waiver meeting. Do not assume Lagos.

### Work and school as a family project

High bachelor’s is a pattern, not a model-minority speech and not proof the elder heard the form.

sections.heading: Religion
sections.body:
Christianity is the large public stream in many southern Nigerian Minnesota households: Pentecostal, Catholic, Anglican. Islam lives in Hausa-Fulani rooms and in some Yoruba families. Traditional practice — Ifá, Odinani, and others — sits in some rooms and is not a souvenir and not horror-film content. None is also a Tuesday. Ask. Do not assume Muslim like Somali. Do not assume Pentecostal.

### Streams

The church is a center of ritual, mutual aid, information, and often the first Minnesota network. It is not “the community.” Do not BCC one pastor and call it consultation. Do not make clergy or an imam the case plan unless this family asked.

### Practice

Funerals gather family and can run long. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Do not treat Ifá or “juju” as a case-note joke. Do not treat a Pentecostal fast as noncompliance with a med until you have asked.

sections.heading: Greetings
sections.body:
Elders first. Titles first in some rooms. English “hello” is ordinary in many professional rooms. Yoruba ẹ n lẹ, Igbo greetings, Hausa sannu live in some rooms. Do not perform tourism greetings as icebreaker. Ask, or follow this room.

### Titles

A hard handshake you assume is universal is already a closed door for some women and some elders. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. If a hand is not offered, nod. Do not force it. Use the title until invited not to.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules onto this page as default. In a Muslim Nigerian room they may apply. Follow this room. Do not assume the Black nod is this grammar.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. Say the name.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
sections.body:
Yoruba names often carry a sentence — Oluwaseun, Adebola, Temitope. Igbo names often carry Chi or Chukwu — Chukwuemeka, Chinwe, Ngozi. Hausa and Muslim names in northern and some Yoruba rooms. English and biblical names sit beside them. A naming ceremony in some families is not folklore. Ask which name they use on this file.

### How to file

U.S. forms want first-middle-last and will strip tones and meaning. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not joke about long names. Do not “shorten” a name for the screen. That invented name becomes a gate.

Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason. Titles are not first names. Do not file Chief as a given name unless they said so.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
sections.body:
Independence Day — 1 October. Schedule around it when this family names it. Guest if invited. A calendar click is not community engagement.

### Calendar

Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa festival calendars this family names — New Yam in some Igbo rooms, Eid in Muslim rooms, Christmas and Easter on church calendars. IgboFest is Minnesota public life. It is not consultation.

Biafra memory for some Igbo rooms is grief and politics, not a party. Do not put it on a case note as color. Do not collect it as a risk score.

Do not put “African holiday” on a case note. Ask this family.

sections.heading: Education
sections.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Nigerian Minnesotans 25 and older, about 96.1 percent high school or higher; about 54.0 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 60.3 percent of the community is foreign-born. High attainment is a documented pattern. It is not a model-minority speech. It is not proof the grandmother needs no interpreter. It is not permission to skip the IEP in the home language.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Yoruba or Igbo and limited Minnesota professional English is not illiterate. Many Nigerians were schooled in English. Some elders were not. LEP 7.6 percent is real. The English-only form is still a gate. Book THIS language. The child is not the interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. Do not treat a physician in the family as proof the waiver household heard the form.

sections.heading: Etiquette
sections.body:
Elders first. Titles. Do not rush a greeting of an elder. Hospitality is a virtue in many rooms. Accept a little food if offered. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Shoes off in some homes. Right hand for food in some rooms. Church time can run long. Do not photograph a family and call it rapport. Do not enter a prayer space as a tour.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. So is a courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
sections.body:
Book the language this household names. Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Edo, Nigerian Pidgin, English, and others. A “Nigerian interpreter” is not a language. An “African interpreter” is a closed door. Pidgin is a language, not broken English. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door. Arabic may be religion, not the interview, in Muslim rooms.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 55.7 percent speak a language other than English; about 7.6 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Low LEP is not proof the form was heard in the language the elder uses for grief and law. Second-generation Minnesota English is common. The IEP still has to reach the parent.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Nigerian coworker the interpreter. Do not write “broken English” on a file.

sections.heading: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice
sections.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Intra-Nigerian politics are real — Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Biafra memory, north and south. Do not pick a side as DHS. Do not referee in a waiver meeting. Do not file politics as a risk score.

FGC exists in some Nigerian communities. Minnesota law stands. Do not invent a Nigerian Minnesota rate. Do not mash Somali prevalence onto this household. Follow mandated reporting. Still see a family.

Colorism sits in some rooms. You do not fix it as a personality. You do not ignore it when it becomes a gate.

Queer and trans Nigerian Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Nigeria’s own law climate is not Minnesota’s. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Enforcement climate is structure for some. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
sections.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent African stoicism. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee. This is not the historic African American page. Shared race is not shared medical history. Do not mash Somali MDH findings onto this people.

### Access

Hepatitis B screening for people born in Nigeria is a U.S. public-health pattern — CDC has treated Nigeria as a higher-prevalence birth country in screening guidance. Date the CDC page you cite. Do not invent a Minnesota rate. Do not skip screening because the person looks well or holds a degree.

Compass disability 8.9 percent — dated. Mental-health stigma is real in some families. Biafra memory and later trauma sit in some rooms. A smile is not a PHQ-9. No dated Nigerian-specific Minnesota autism rate belongs on this page. Do not invent one.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Traditional medicine and church healing often sit beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. FGC: Minnesota law stands; do not invent a rate; do not skip care. High education is not a clinical history.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
sections.body:
Queer and trans Nigerian Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, Pentecostal, Catholic, and mosque climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Yoruba or Igbo life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. Nigeria’s law climate is not this state’s. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

Biafra memory and church do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
sections.body:
Gele, iro and buba, agbada, isiagu, and other ceremonial dress are public at weddings, Independence, IgboFest, and some church stages. They are not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

This is not the CROWN Act chapter as the file — and anti-Blackness still sits on Nigerian bodies in U.S. clinics, schools, and traffic stops. Ask this person. Do not mash historic African American hair politics as a script, and do not ignore them.

Do not touch. Gold, a gele, a wedding coral — not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

sections.heading: Music
sections.body:
Jùjú, fuji, highlife, Igbo gospel, Hausa popular forms, Afrobeats, Nollywood sound, church choir. Named variation, not a playlist. Ethnic and political memory can sit inside a song. You do not put the wrong anthem on a speaker.

### Variation

A funeral is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement. Nollywood is public culture. It is not consultation and not a case plan.

Independence and IgboFest stages are public life. They are not a form.

sections.heading: Sports
sections.body:
Soccer is public Nigerian life. Super Eagles are a public image. They are not a personality you assign a child in clinic. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Basketball shows up.

### Not the whole person

Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see. Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some. They are not language access and not a case plan.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday if this elder needs Yoruba or Igbo.

sections.heading: Literature
sections.body:
English, Yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa made written publics. Chinua Achebe, Wole Soyinka, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie are literacy for the desk, not a speech you give the family in the lobby. Oral forms sit beside them. Minnesota and U.S. Nigerian writers and journalists exist.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do need to know this is not a people without letters. Many people read English. Some elders read only a home language. A notice that exists only in English is a closed door. High bachelor’s is not proof this elder reads the form.

Write what they tell you. Do not strip a name because the screen is impatient.

sections.heading: Art
sections.body:
Adire, bronze as a public image of a court, gele, contemporary visual work, Nollywood. Jollof, pounded yam, and egusi are foodway, not consultation.

### Guest
